        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update on x_casemgmt_case: when previous.status == 'Resolved' AND current.status == 'Closed', sets current.closed_date = gs.nowDateTime() if not already populated. Replaces ArkCase ChangeCaseFileStateService.changeCaseState() retval.setClosed(now) (line 99 in acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (Resolved->Closed auto-sets closed_date) and AAP Section 0.5.7 (closed_date DateTime, Auto-set on Close transition). Order=500 ensures this rule runs LAST among before-update rules so it only fires after all transition guards (block_terminal_closed, block_draft_backtransition, validate_assigned_agent_membership, clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress) have passed. Defensive .nil() guard preserves authoritative pre-set values from seed data and the validate_closed_transition Flow Designer subflow. Defense in depth with the subflow is intentional - this BR catches direct DB updates (Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts), the subflow catches interactive transitions through the form/UI. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_set_closed_date</name>
        <order>500</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase
    // ChangeCaseFileStateService.changeCaseState() line 99:
    //     if ("CLOSED".equals(newState)) { retval.setClosed(now); }
    // (acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    //  armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java)
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5: Resolved -> Closed transition auto-sets closed_date.
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7: closed_date is "DateTime, Auto-set on Close transition".
    //
    // This BR runs alongside the Flow Designer subflow
    // ../flows/sub_flows/validate_closed_transition.xml; the redundancy is
    // intentional - this BR catches direct DB modifications (Table API,
    // scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts, bulk imports), the flow catches
    // interactive transitions through the form/UI.
    //
    // Order=500 makes this the LAST before-update rule on the table
    // (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at
    // order=200, enforce_forward_transitions at order=250,
    // validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300,
    // clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at order=400 all run first).
    //
    // Running last is NOT the same as being skipped when an earlier rule
    // rejects the save. setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE; the platform
    // still runs this rule, and only current.isActionAborted() reveals the
    // pending abort. That is exactly how a denied Resolved -> Closed
    // previously produced a phantom Closed Date on the redisplayed form: the
    // order-250 rule had refused the transition, this rule ran anyway and
    // stamped the in-memory record, and the user saw a closed date on a case
    // the database still held as Resolved. The explicit guard below closes
    // that gap - closed_date is never stamped on a transition that is about
    // to be rejected.
    //
    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null in
    // certain async/system contexts. If there is no previous state, no
    // transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing. The String()
    // cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string for safe
    // === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string equality
    // can behave inconsistently across releases.
    var prevStatus = previous ? String(previous.status) : '';
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Verbatim Title Case status values per AAP Section 0.5.7 and the
    // sibling choice list ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml. The
    // labels ARE the stored values - ServiceNow Choice fields persist
    // the LABEL string by default, not an integer ID.
    if (prevStatus === 'Resolved' && newStatus === 'Closed') {
        // Do not stamp a rejected save. The order-250 rule refuses a close
        // attempted by a non-manager with "Only case managers can close
        // cases." and calls setAbortAction(true); the platform still runs
        // this rule, so without this check the redisplayed form would show a
        // Closed Date for a case that remains Resolved in the database.
        if (current.isActionAborted()) {
            return;
        }

        // Defensive .nil() guard: respect pre-set values from the
        // Flow Designer subflow (which fires in the same transaction
        // for interactive transitions and may have already stamped
        // the column) and from any future seed-data path that updates
        // an already-loaded case from Resolved to Closed. Without this
        // guard, a value already written by the subflow would be
        // overwritten by gs.nowDateTime() at this rule's execution
        // point - harmless in practice (both writers produce the same
        // millisecond-precision timestamp within a single transaction)
        // but unnecessary and slightly less clear in audit logs.
        if (current.closed_date.nil()) {
            current.closed_date = new GlideDateTime();
        }
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name>

sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>true</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-insert/update on x_casemgmt_case: when assigned_agent and assigned_group are both populated, validates that the agent is a member of the group via x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.isAgentInGroup(). On failure, surfaces the form-level error 'Assigned agent must be a member of the assigned group.' via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true). Per AAP Sections 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 2: Open -> In Progress: 'assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group') and 0.5.7 (assigned_agent constraint: 'Optional; must be member of assigned_group'). Order=300 places this rule THIRD in the before-rule chain on x_casemgmt_case, after block_terminal_closed (100) and block_draft_backtransition (200) and before clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress (400) and set_closed_date (500); running after the prohibition guards is a deliberate performance optimization so we don't run the sys_user_grmember GlideRecord lookup on transitions that will be rejected anyway. Dual-triggered (action_insert=true AND action_update=true) because a manager (or seed script) may assign agent and group at case-creation time via a single Table API call, not just through subsequent updates. Skip conditions: (a) either agent or group is empty (b) neither field changed since previous - avoid redundant queries on non-assignment-touching updates. Defensive previous-null guard: on insert previous is null and both change-detection flags evaluate true so the membership is always validated for new rows. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types because the membership constraint applies regardless of case type. Defense in depth: validate_inprogress_transition subflow makes the same check at the workflow layer; this BR catches direct DB writes bypassing the flow. The error message wording is NOT prescribed verbatim by AAP Section 0.7.4 (which lists only four verbatim messages); the chosen wording is consistent with the prompt's tone and the AAP's own narrative wording. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals (runtime sys_id comparisons via .toString() are platform-canonical and permitted).</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership</name>
        <order>300</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7 (x_casemgmt_case schema row 10):
    //     "assigned_agent | Reference -> sys_user | Optional; must be
    //      member of assigned_group"
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 2):
    //     | From | To          | Required condition                       | Failure handling          |
    //     | Open | In Progress | assigned_agent populated AND member of   | Surface form-level error  |
    //     |      |             | assigned_group                           |                           |
    //
    // The membership check is delegated to
    //     new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator().isAgentInGroup(agentSysId, groupSysId)
    // which performs a sys_user_grmember GlideRecord lookup and returns a
    // plain boolean. The Script Include is the single source of truth for
    // the membership query so the same logic is reusable across this BR,
    // the validate_inprogress_transition Flow Designer subflow, ACL
    // conditions for child case_task and case_party rows, and the
    // seed-script preflight checks. Inlining a GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember')
    // query here would create a second source of truth and risk the two
    // implementations diverging on edge cases.
    //
    // Order=300 places this rule in the before-rule chain on x_casemgmt_case
    // after block_terminal_closed (order=100, blocks any edit to a Closed
    // case), block_draft_backtransition (order=200, blocks any rewind to
    // Draft) and enforce_forward_transitions (order=250, enforces the forward
    // preconditions).
    //
    // Order alone is NOT a short circuit. setAbortAction(true) cancels the
    // WRITE; the platform still runs every remaining before-update rule and
    // reports the pending abort through current.isActionAborted(). Ordering
    // therefore decides only whose message is added first. The explicit
    // abort-state guard below is what keeps this rule from adding a second
    // message to a save that an earlier rule already rejected - and the same
    // guard is present in the order-400 and order-500 rules.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: there was no direct equivalent at the JPA
    // entity layer in
    //   acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/
    //     com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java
    // CaseFile modeled assignment via an AcmParticipant collection (lines
    // 192, 336-340, 880-908) where ASSIGNEE and OWNING_GROUP participant
    // types coexisted on the case but the relational integrity between an
    // assignee and the owning group was enforced indirectly through the
    // LDAP/AD organizational structure - if a user existed in LDAP they
    // could be assigned regardless of their group membership. The
    // ServiceNow target makes this rule EXPLICIT at the data layer via
    // this BR plus the Script Include's isAgentInGroup() helper - a
    // deliberate hardening of the case assignment contract. This is a
    // TARGET-SIDE AUTHORED rule with no byte-for-byte source analog.

    // Read the assigned_agent and assigned_group sys_id values from the
    // platform-injected `current` GlideRecord. The .toString() coercion
    // normalizes the GlideElement reference field to its underlying sys_id
    // string. Without explicit coercion, the GlideElement instance auto-
    // converts in some contexts but not others (string concatenation =
    // string conversion; equality comparison via === = identity comparison;
    // method-argument passing = pass-by-value of the underlying string
    // for primitive comparisons but pass-by-reference of the GlideElement
    // wrapper for complex operations). The downstream isAgentInGroup()
    // method explicitly handles String() coercion of its arguments and
    // GlideRecord.addQuery() accepts both forms, but explicit .toString()
    // here is the platform-canonical defensive pattern and avoids any
    // wrapper-vs-primitive ambiguity downstream.
    var agent = current.assigned_agent.toString();
    var group = current.assigned_group.toString();

    // Skip if either field is empty. The AAP defines assigned_agent as
    // optional (Section 0.5.7: "Optional"); a case without an assigned
    // agent is a valid state (e.g., Draft cases, Open cases waiting for
    // agent assignment). assigned_group is mandatory only on the
    // Open transition (per dictionary mandatory_on_open=true at
    // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_assigned_group.xml) - that mandatory
    // requirement is enforced separately by the form-level mandatory flag
    // and the validate_open_transition subflow, NOT by this BR.
    // This BR's responsibility is narrow: validate the membership
    // RELATIONSHIP when both fields are present. If either field is
    // absent, the relationship cannot be validated and the rule does
    // nothing.
    if (!agent || !group) {
        return;
    }

    // Skip if neither agent nor group changed (avoid redundant queries on
    // every save, including subsequent updates that touch only other
    // fields like description, priority, or status). For a case that
    // travels through the full state-machine
    //   Draft -> Open -> In Progress -> Pending -> In Progress -> Resolved -> Closed
    // the assignment fields typically change at most twice (once when the
    // group is set on Draft -> Open, once when the agent is set on
    // Open -> In Progress). This guard ensures the BR runs the
    // sys_user_grmember query at most twice across the full lifecycle
    // rather than five times.
    //
    // On INSERT, `previous` is null (no prior state), so the ternary's
    // !previous branch evaluates true for both flags - the BR always
    // validates the membership on a brand-new row. This is the correct
    // semantic: a manager creating a case AND assigning both group and
    // agent in a single operation must have the assignment validated
    // before the row is persisted, otherwise an invalid agent-group
    // pairing could be created and only caught on the first subsequent
    // update.
    var agentChanged = !previous || String(previous.assigned_agent) !== agent;
    var groupChanged = !previous || String(previous.assigned_group) !== group;
    if (!agentChanged && !groupChanged) {
        return;
    }

    // Skip if an earlier rule in the chain has already rejected this save.
    // The platform continues running before-update rules after
    // setAbortAction(true) and exposes the pending abort through
    // current.isActionAborted(). Returning here keeps a rejected transition
    // (for example Closed -> * refused at order 100, or a forward
    // precondition refused at order 250) from collecting a second, unrelated
    // membership message on top of the message the user needs to read, and
    // avoids a sys_user_grmember query for a row that will never be written.
    if (current.isActionAborted()) {
        return;
    }

    // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
    // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
    // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the
    // `CaseTransitionValidator` portion is the api_name of the Script
    // Include declared in
    // ../script_includes/x_casemgmt_CaseTransitionValidator.xml at
    // <api_name>x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator</api_name>. NO sys_id
    // literal - the resolution is by scoped class name only.
    var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();

    // Call isAgentInGroup(userSysId, groupSysId). The Script Include's
    // method (line 656 in CaseTransitionValidator.xml) returns a plain
    // boolean: true when at least one sys_user_grmember row links the
    // given user to the given group, false otherwise (including when
    // either argument is null/empty/whitespace). The boolean shape
    // (rather than the {ok, error} pair used by validateNoBacktransition
    // and the canTransitionTo* family) is intentional: isAgentInGroup is
    // a simple yes/no membership predicate reusable from contexts that
    // have no error-message surface (e.g., ACL condition expressions).
    // The form-level error string is owned by THIS BR and surfaced via
    // gs.addErrorMessage(...) below.
    if (!validator.isAgentInGroup(agent, group)) {
        // gs.addErrorMessage('...') surfaces the form-level error at the
        // top of the case form when the user attempts the save through
        // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
        // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. Per AAP Section 0.7.1:
        // "Surface all blocking errors on the form. Invalid transition
        // attempts MUST produce a blocking error message visible on the
        // form - silent failures or post-save error logs are
        // unacceptable."
        //
        // Per AAP Section 0.7.4, only four error messages are verbatim
        // (non-negotiable): "All tasks must be closed before resolving
        // this case.", "Cases cannot be returned to Draft.", "Closed
        // cases are terminal and cannot be modified.", and "No case
        // found with that number." This rule's message is NOT in that
        // list, so the wording here is target-side authored. The chosen
        // string is consistent with the prompt's tone and the AAP's own
        // narrative wording in Section 0.5.7 ("Optional; must be member
        // of assigned_group").
        gs.addErrorMessage('Assigned agent must be a member of the assigned group.');

        // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
        // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
        // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
        // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
        // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
        // would still update with the invalid agent-group pairing;
        // without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write would be silently
        // rejected with no visible failure and no diagnostic message
        // for the caller.
        current.setAbortAction(true);
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>

sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>false</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update on x_casemgmt_case: when previous.status == 'Pending' AND current.status == 'In Progress', clears current.pending_reason (sets it to empty string). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (Pending->In Progress: clears pending_reason). Order=400 ensures this rule runs after the transition guards (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at order=200, validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300) but before set_closed_date (order=500), so it only fires after all guards have approved the transition. Companion to ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml which SETS pending_reason on the In Progress->Pending transition; this rule CLEARS it on the reverse transition. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types since the Pending state is shared. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero GlideRecord lookups.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress</name>
        <order>400</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 verbatim:
    //     "Pending -> In Progress: None; clears pending_reason"
    //
    // The pending_reason field is SET by the Flow Designer subflow
    // ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml when the case
    // transitions INTO Pending. When the case transitions OUT of Pending
    // back to In Progress, the previously stored reason is no longer
    // relevant and would be misleading on the form. This rule guarantees
    // the field is empty for any non-Pending case reached via the
    // Pending -> In Progress transition path.
    //
    // This BR has no ArkCase source-side analog. ArkCase did not have
    // a discrete Pending sub-state with a typed reason code; this is
    // target-side-only behavior introduced by the AAP design.
    //
    // Order=400 places this rule after the transition guards
    // (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at
    // order=200, enforce_forward_transitions at order=250,
    // validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300) and before
    // set_closed_date (order=500), which handles the Resolved -> Closed
    // side-effect.
    //
    // Order alone does NOT skip this rule when an earlier guard rejects the
    // save: setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, and the platform keeps
    // running the rest of the before-update chain, reporting the pending
    // abort through current.isActionAborted(). The explicit guard below is
    // what prevents pending_reason from being cleared on the in-memory record
    // of a transition that is about to be rejected - without it the
    // redisplayed form would show an empty Pending Reason for a case that
    // still holds one in the database.
    //
    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null
    // in certain async/system contexts. If there is no previous state,
    // no transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing. The
    // String() cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string
    // for safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string
    // equality can behave inconsistently across releases.
    var prevStatus = previous ? String(previous.status) : '';
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Verbatim Title Case status values per AAP Section 0.5.7 and the
    // sibling choice list ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml. The
    // labels ARE the stored values - ServiceNow Choice fields persist
    // the LABEL string by default, not an integer ID. Note 'In Progress'
    // contains a literal SPACE in the middle (NOT 'In_Progress', NOT
    // 'InProgress', NOT 'in progress'). Misspelled variants would
    // silently never match and the rule would never fire - a critical
    // correctness concern that is encoded by these exact string literals.
    if (prevStatus === 'Pending' && newStatus === 'In Progress') {
        // Do not mutate a rejected save. An earlier before-update rule may
        // have called setAbortAction(true); the platform still runs this rule
        // and only current.isActionAborted() reveals that state. Clearing the
        // field here would leave the redisplayed form contradicting the
        // database.
        if (current.isActionAborted()) {
            return;
        }

        // The empty-string assignment is the canonical ServiceNow pattern
        // for clearing a Choice field's value. Per
        // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_pending_reason.xml the field is
        // non-mandatory (mandatory=false), so clearing it is a legitimate
        // end-state - the row remains valid with an empty pending_reason
        // for any non-Pending status. The next time the case transitions
        // to Pending, the validate_pending_transition subflow will prompt
        // for a fresh reason and populate the field again.
        current.pending_reason = '';
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name>

        <sys_policy/>

        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <template/>
        <when>before</when>
    </sys_script>
</record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_cbea5a36ef6efe5a077e0548c45468ce
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>false</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update guard on x_casemgmt_case that enforces the forward-transition preconditions of the case state machine. On a status change it invokes the matching natively authored Flow Designer subflow (x_casemgmt.validate_open_transition, validate_in_progress_transition, validate_pending_transition, validate_resolved_transition, validate_closed_transition) synchronously with sn_fd.FlowAPI.getRunner().inForeground(), then re-evaluates the same gate against the in-flight record through x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator and, on failure, calls gs.addErrorMessage() with the verbatim blocking message plus current.setAbortAction(true) so the error surfaces on the form. Order 250 runs after the Closed-terminal (100) and Any-to-Draft (200) prohibition guards and before the side-effect rules (300/400/500). FAIL-CLOSED: the six canonical statuses are an explicit allowlist - Draft passes to the order-200 rule that owns it, the other five are gated here, and any other value (a stale choice, a direct Table API or scripted write such as Approved) is refused with a blocking message and setAbortAction(true) rather than skipping every gate; and validator construction, guard dispatch and verdict-shape validation all run inside one try/catch, so an exception, a malformed verdict, a non-boolean ok or a rejection with no message produces an explicit deny with a sanitized server diagnostic and a generic user message instead of relying on platform exception semantics.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions</name>
        <order>250</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script>(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Guard against the INSERT path. `previous` is null on insert, and a
    // brand-new case has no prior status, so there is no forward
    // transition to validate. Portal submissions insert with
    // status = Draft and must never be blocked here.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (!previous) {
        return;
    }

    var previousStatus = String(previous.status);
    var proposedStatus = String(current.status);

    // Only a genuine status change is a transition. Field-only updates
    // (subject, description, priority, assignment) are not this rule's
    // concern and are left to the other before-update rules.
    if (previousStatus === proposedStatus) {
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Stop if an earlier rule in the chain has already rejected this save.
    //
    // setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, not the remaining before-update
    // rules - the platform keeps running them and reports the pending abort
    // through current.isActionAborted(). Order 100
    // (x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed, Closed -> *) and order 200
    // (x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition, Any -> Draft) both run first and
    // both abort with their own verbatim message. Returning here means an
    // already-rejected transition does not pay the 8-10 second synchronous
    // subflow execution below, and does not collect a second diagnosis for a
    // save that will never be persisted.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (current.isActionAborted()) {
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Map the proposed status onto the Flow Designer subflow that owns
    // its precondition. The subflow internal names are the natively
    // authored subflows in this scope; each one runs the shared
    // `Case Transition Guard` Custom Action, which delegates to
    // x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator so there is a single source of
    // truth for the transition rules and their verbatim messages.
    //
    // 'Draft' is deliberately absent: the Any -> Draft prohibition is
    // owned by x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition (order 200) and the
    // Closed -> * prohibition by x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed
    // (order 100). Both run before this rule.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var SUBFLOW_FOR_STATUS = {
        'Open': 'validate_open_transition',
        'In Progress': 'validate_in_progress_transition',
        'Pending': 'validate_pending_transition',
        'Resolved': 'validate_resolved_transition',
        'Closed': 'validate_closed_transition'
    };
    var subflowName = SUBFLOW_FOR_STATUS[proposedStatus];
    if (!subflowName) {
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // ALLOWLIST, NOT A LOOKUP MISS. Reaching here means the proposed
        // status is not one of the five this rule dispatches on. Exactly one
        // value legitimately lands here - 'Draft' - because the Any -> Draft
        // prohibition belongs to x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition at
        // order 200, which has already aborted the save with its own verbatim
        // message. Every OTHER value is a status this application does not
        // recognise, and it must NOT be allowed through.
        //
        // Why this matters: a mandatory Choice dictionary is not a server-side
        // allowlist. ServiceNow stores and displays a value that is not (or is
        // no longer) a valid choice, and a direct write - Table API, a scoped
        // script, an import - can set `status` to anything at all. Returning
        // without aborting, as an earlier revision did, let such a write park a
        // case in an unrecognised state with NO assignment check, NO task
        // closure check and NO manager check: every order-250 gate skipped.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        if (proposedStatus === 'Draft') {
            return;
        }
        // The offending value is recorded server-side, sanitized (newlines
        // stripped, length capped) so a crafted value cannot forge log lines,
        // and is deliberately NOT echoed back to the user.
        var sanitized = proposedStatus.replace(/[\r\n\t]+/g, ' ');
        if (sanitized.length > 80) {
            sanitized = sanitized.substring(0, 80) + '...';
        }
        gs.error('x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions: refused a status this application does not' +
                 ' recognise on case ' + String(current.getUniqueValue()) + ' (' + previousStatus +
                 ' -> "' + sanitized + '"). Only Draft, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved and Closed' +
                 ' are valid; the write was aborted.');
        gs.addErrorMessage('That is not a valid case status. A case may only be Draft, Open, In Progress, ' +
                           'Pending, Resolved or Closed.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    var caseSysId = String(current.getUniqueValue());

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // STEP 1 - run the Flow Designer subflow SYNCHRONOUSLY.
    //
    // Flow Designer record triggers (Created / Updated) fire AFTER the
    // database write commits, so a triggered flow can never abort a save
    // or surface a form-level blocking error. Invoking the subflow in the
    // foreground from this before-update rule is what makes the
    // state-machine flows load-bearing at the moment of the transition
    // instead of after it.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var flowBlocked = null;
    try {
        var flowOutputs = sn_fd.FlowAPI.getRunner()
            .subflow('x_casemgmt.' + subflowName)
            .inForeground()
            .withInputs({ case_sys_id: caseSysId })
            .run()
            .getOutputs();
        flowBlocked = (String(flowOutputs['blocked']) === 'true');
    } catch (flowError) {
        // Fail closed onto the validator rather than silently allowing
        // the transition: STEP 2 below still decides the outcome.
        gs.warn('x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions: subflow x_casemgmt.' + subflowName +
                ' could not be executed for case ' + caseSysId + ' - ' + flowError +
                '. Falling back to the in-flight CaseTransitionValidator evaluation.');
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // STEP 2 - evaluate the same gate against the IN-FLIGHT record.
    //
    // The subflow reads the case from the database, so it sees the
    // committed row. A single save may change `assigned_group` or
    // `assigned_agent` in the same transaction as `status`; in that case
    // the committed row is stale and only `current` reflects what will
    // actually be persisted. This step therefore decides the outcome,
    // using the identical x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator methods the
    // subflow's Custom Action calls, so both paths produce the same
    // verbatim messages. For a status-only save - which is what all six
    // UI Actions and the case form produce - the two verdicts are
    // identical and the subflow's verdict IS the decision.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Everything that decides the outcome is inside this try/catch, because
    // this is the load-bearing authorization step for a direct update and it
    // must fail CLOSED. Constructing the Script Include can throw (a scope
    // resolution failure, a compile error in the include, an upgrade in
    // flight); the guards themselves run GlideRecord and GlideAggregate
    // queries against sys_user_grmember, sys_user_has_role and
    // x_casemgmt_case_task, any of which can throw or time out; and a future
    // edit could return something that is not a verdict at all. Without this
    // wrapper any of those exits before the only explicit
    // current.setAbortAction(true) below, and enforcement would then depend on
    // platform exception semantics rather than on a deny decision this rule
    // actually took.
    var verdict;
    try {
        var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
        if (proposedStatus === 'Open') {
            verdict = validator.canTransitionToOpen(current);
        } else if (proposedStatus === 'In Progress') {
            verdict = validator.canTransitionToInProgress(current);
        } else if (proposedStatus === 'Resolved') {
            verdict = validator.canTransitionToResolved(current);
        } else if (proposedStatus === 'Closed') {
            verdict = validator.canTransitionToClosed(current, gs.getUserID());
        } else {
            // 'Pending' carries no precondition per the transition matrix.
            verdict = { ok: true };
        }
        // VERDICT SHAPE IS VALIDATED, NOT ASSUMED. A missing verdict, a
        // non-object, a non-boolean `ok`, or a rejection with no message would
        // all read as "allowed" or as a blank blocking error, i.e. a silent
        // failure - which AAP Section 0.7.1 forbids.
        if (!verdict || typeof verdict !== 'object' || typeof verdict.ok !== 'boolean') {
            throw 'the validator returned a malformed verdict for ' + previousStatus + ' -> ' +
                  proposedStatus + ' (' + String(verdict) + ')';
        }
        if (verdict.ok === false && (typeof verdict.error !== 'string' || verdict.error === '')) {
            throw 'the validator rejected ' + previousStatus + ' -> ' + proposedStatus +
                  ' without supplying a message';
        }
    } catch (validatorError) {
        // Deny, explicitly. The diagnostic goes to the server log; the user
        // gets a generic message that leaks no internals.
        gs.error('x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions: the transition guard could not be evaluated for' +
                 ' case ' + caseSysId + ' (' + previousStatus + ' -> ' + proposedStatus + ') - ' +
                 validatorError + '. The save was aborted: an unevaluated transition is refused, never' +
                 ' allowed.');
        gs.addErrorMessage('This change could not be validated and has not been saved. Please try again, ' +
                           'and tell your administrator if it keeps happening.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // Record any divergence so an operator can see when a combined
    // field-and-status save made the committed row stale.
    if (flowBlocked !== null && flowBlocked !== !verdict.ok) {
        gs.info('x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions: subflow x_casemgmt.' + subflowName +
                ' reported blocked=' + flowBlocked + ' while the in-flight evaluation reported blocked=' +
                (!verdict.ok) + ' for case ' + caseSysId + ' (' + previousStatus + ' -> ' + proposedStatus +
                '). The in-flight evaluation decides because it reflects the row as it will be saved.');
    }

    if (!verdict.ok) {
        // VERBATIM message from CaseTransitionValidator - do not paraphrase.
        gs.addErrorMessage(verdict.error);
        current.setAbortAction(true);
    }
})(current, previous);
</script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>

true party_typeISNOTEMPTY^ORparty_typeISEMPTY^EQ Polymorphic field-rendering UI Policy on x_casemgmt_case_party. Implements the ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase's @DiscriminatorColumn(cm_class_name) single-table inheritance pattern from PersonAssociation.java and the dual-table @ManyToOne pattern from PersonOrganizationAssociation.java per AAP Section 0.4.3 ("Polymorphic association via single-table choice + UI Policy"). Uses run_scripts=true with an imperative onCondition script to deterministically set field visibility and mandatory state for all three party_type values: "Person" (show person + mandatory; hide organization), "Organization" (show organization + mandatory; hide person), and empty (hide both fields, both not mandatory). The script_true block is the sole logic path; no declarative actions are used because the declarative two-policy approach with reverse_if_false=true has an unavoidable order-conflict in the empty-state case. Runs on form load (on_load=true) so existing case_party records render correctly when opened. The party_type field itself is mandatory at the dictionary level (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_party_party_type.xml), so users cannot save a record without picking one; the mandatory state of person/organization is therefore conditional on party_type and enforced ONLY through this UI Policy. true false Case Party Conditional Fields true 100 false true Polymorphic field rendering: show person+mandatory when party_type=Person, show organization+mandatory when party_type=Organization, hide both when party_type is empty. sys_ui_policy admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global 854295ebb4c8309eea6a52aa788ec8a9 0 x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case_party

x_casemgmt_case_open true false UI Action that transitions a Draft case to Open status. Visible only to x_casemgmt_case_manager users on cases with status=Draft. Delegates the assigned_group-populated check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToOpen() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_open_transition.xml). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 1 verbatim: "Draft -> Open: assigned_group populated - Surface form-level error". Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the assigned_group field that the operator should have populated on the form before clicking. Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role and status. sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_ws_operation">
    <sys_ws_operation action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <active>true</active>
        <consumes>application/json</consumes>
        <consumes_customized>true</consumes_customized>
        <default_operation_uri>/api/x_casemgmt/case_submit</default_operation_uri>
        <description>POST handler for the Case Submit scripted REST API. Anonymously accepts a JSON payload containing the whitelisted fields { subject, type, description, requester_name, requester_email } from the Experience Portal submission widget. Delegates to x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.submitCase() which inserts a new x_casemgmt_case row with status=Draft and silently drops any non-whitelisted fields. On success, returns HTTP 201 with body { number, message: 'Your case has been submitted' }. On validation failure, returns HTTP 400 with body { error }. On defensive fallback (Script Include returned no number and no error - should never happen if the Script Include conforms to its contract), returns HTTP 500 with body { error: 'Submission failed.' }. Replaces ArkCase's DefaultPluggablePortalRequestService.submitRequest() Spring service for the Case Submit slice. Anonymous access is enabled by setting requires_authentication=false, requires_acl_authorization=false, and requires_snc_internal_role=false; the privacy perimeter is the field whitelist in the Script Include, not table-level ACLs. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 0.5.1, 0.7.4 (verbatim).</description>
        <enforce_acl/>
        <http_method>POST</http_method>
        <name>Case Submit POST</name>
        <operation_script>(function process(/*RESTAPIRequest*/ request, /*RESTAPIResponse*/ response) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.4.3 + Section 0.4.4 + Section 0.7.4:
    // Anonymous case-submission endpoint. The whitelisted-field discipline
    // (input fields restricted to subject, type, description, requester_name,
    // requester_email) plus the forced status='Draft' enforcement live in
    // the Script Include x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.submitCase(). This
    // handler is intentionally thin: only HTTP-layer concerns (status codes,
    // body shapes, payload extraction) live here.
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.4.4 (verbatim, non-negotiable): the success
    // response includes the message text 'Your case has been submitted'.
    // The submission widget displays this text verbatim in its confirmation
    // panel; paraphrasing would break the AAP contract.

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1. Extract the JSON payload defensively.
    //
    //    request.body may be undefined (no body supplied - rare but
    //    possible if a malicious client sends POST with no Content-Type
    //    or empty body).
    //    request.body.data is the auto-parsed JSON object when the
    //    Content-Type is application/json (per <consumes>application/json
    //    </consumes> on this operation). It may be undefined if the body
    //    failed to parse.
    //    Pass null to the Script Include when either is missing - the
    //    Script Include's defensive type-check returns
    //    { error: 'Invalid payload.' } which this handler translates to
    //    HTTP 400.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    var payload = request.body && request.body.data ? request.body.data : null;

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2. Delegate to the Script Include. The Script Include is the single
    //    source of truth for:
    //      - The field whitelist (only subject, type, description,
    //        requester_name, requester_email accepted)
    //      - The status='Draft' force (regardless of payload contents)
    //      - The GlideRecord.insert() call against x_casemgmt_case
    //      - The post-insert re-query for the auto-generated number
    //
    //    Contract:
    //      - submitCase(payload) returns:
    //          * { error: '<message>' }   - validation/insert failure
    //          * { number: 'CASE0000001' } - success, auto-generated number
    //
    //    The Script Include is invoked via the scope-qualified API name
    //    `x_casemgmt.CasePortalService` (NOT by sys_id), which complies
    //    with AAP Section 0.7.2's no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    var svc = new x_casemgmt.CasePortalService();
    var result = svc.submitCase(payload);

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3. Validation failure -> HTTP 400 Bad Request.
    //
    //    The Script Include returns { error: 'Invalid payload.' } when
    //    the payload is null/non-object/array, and
    //    { error: 'Submission failed.' } when GlideRecord.insert() rejects
    //    the row (typically a before-insert BR rejection or a missing
    //    mandatory field). Both surface as HTTP 400 to give the calling
    //    widget actionable feedback.
    //
    //    String() coercion on result.error defends against a future
    //    refactor that returns a non-string error value (e.g., an Error
    //    object); the JSON serializer would otherwise produce
    //    unpredictable output.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (result && result.error) {
        response.setStatus(400);
        response.setBody({ error: String(result.error) });
        return;
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4. Defensive fallback -> HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.
    //
    //    This branch should NEVER trigger if the Script Include conforms
    //    to its contract (always returns either { number } or { error }).
    //    The fallback exists for production reliability:
    //      - If a future refactor breaks the Script Include's contract,
    //        the handler returns a clean 500 rather than serializing
    //        undefined or throwing an uncaught error.
    //      - The error message is intentionally generic ('Submission
    //        failed.') to avoid leaking implementation details to
    //        anonymous callers.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (!result || !result.number) {
        response.setStatus(500);
        response.setBody({ error: 'Submission failed.' });
        return;
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 5. Success -> HTTP 201 Created with { number, message }.
    //
    //    HTTP 201 (vs 200): REST convention - 201 indicates a NEW
    //    resource was created on the server. The submission widget can
    //    rely on this status code to distinguish successful creation
    //    from any other 2xx outcome.
    //
    //    Response body shape (exactly two keys, no others):
    //      {
    //        number:  '<auto-generated CASE0000001-format string>',
    //        message: 'Your case has been submitted'
    //      }
    //
    //    String(result.number) coercion defends against any future
    //    GlideElement-typed return value (the Script Include already
    //    coerces with String(savedGr.getValue('number')), but this
    //    handler-level coercion is defense-in-depth).
    //
    //    The verbatim message 'Your case has been submitted' matches AAP
    //    Section 0.4.4: "displays a confirmation panel showing the
    //    returned case number and a friendly 'Your case has been
    //    submitted' message". The widget displays this text verbatim
    //    in its confirmation panel.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    response.setStatus(201);
    response.setBody({
        number: String(result.number),
        message: 'Your case has been submitted'
    });
})(request, response);</operation_script>
        <operation_uri>/api/x_casemgmt/case_submit</operation_uri>
        <produces>application/json</produces>
        <produces_customized>true</produces_customized>
        <relative_path>/</relative_path>
        <request_example/>
        <requires_acl_authorization>false</requires_acl_authorization>
        <requires_authentication>false</requires_authentication>
        <requires_snc_internal_role>false</requires_snc_internal_role>
        <short_description>Anonymous POST handler for case submission. Returns HTTP 201 with { number, message: 'Your case has been submitted' } on success, HTTP 400 with { error } on validation failure, or HTTP 500 with { error: 'Submission failed.' } on defensive fallback. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 0.5.1, 0.7.4.</short_description>
        <sys_class_name>sys_ws_operation</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2026-04-30 12:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>886ad7128907a6351ea04b210c27029e</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_name>Case Submit POST</sys_name>
        <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package>
        <sys_policy/>
        <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope>
        <sys_update_name>sys_ws_operation_x_casemgmt_case_submit_post</sys_update_name>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2026-04-30 12:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <web_service_definition display_value="x_casemgmt_case_submit">ef9090a5b03f1a36c248ce65065a1b74</web_service_definition>
        <web_service_version/>
    </sys_ws_operation>
</record_update>

<record_update table="sys_ws_operation">
    <sys_ws_operation action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <active>true</active>
        <consumes>application/json</consumes>
        <consumes_customized>true</consumes_customized>
        <default_operation_uri>/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup</default_operation_uri>
        <description>GET handler for the Case Status Lookup scripted REST API. Anonymously accepts a case number via the 'number' query parameter from the Experience Portal lookup widget. Delegates to x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.lookupCase() which queries x_casemgmt_case by number and returns ONLY the whitelisted fields { status, subject, opened_date } - never assigned_group, assigned_agent, description, closed_date, requester_* fields, priority, type, pending_reason, or any audit field. On match, returns HTTP 200 with body { status, subject, opened_date }. On no match (or empty/missing query parameter), returns HTTP 404 with the verbatim body { error: 'No case found with that number.' } per AAP Section 0.7.4. Replaces ArkCase's GetCaseByNumberServiceImpl.getCaseByNumber() Spring service. Anonymous access is enabled by setting requires_authentication=false, requires_acl_authorization=false, and requires_snc_internal_role=false; the privacy perimeter is the field whitelist in the Script Include, not table-level ACLs.</description>
        <enforce_acl/>
        <http_method>GET</http_method>
        <name>Case Status Lookup GET</name>
        <operation_script>(function process(/*RESTAPIRequest*/ request, /*RESTAPIResponse*/ response) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.4.4 + Section 0.7.4 (Other User-Provided Rules):
    // Anonymous case-status-lookup endpoint. The whitelisted-field discipline
    // (response contains ONLY status, subject, opened_date) lives in the
    // Script Include x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.lookupCase(). This handler
    // is intentionally thin: only HTTP-layer concerns (status codes, body
    // shapes, query-parameter extraction) live here.
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.7.4 (verbatim, non-negotiable): when the case number
    // does NOT match, return HTTP 404 with the verbatim body
    //   { error: 'No case found with that number.' }
    // The EXACT text (capital N, lowercase elsewhere, trailing period,
    // ASCII straight single quotes) is mandated by AAP Sections 0.4.4 and
    // 0.7.4. The lookup widget displays this text verbatim.

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1. Extract the 'number' query parameter defensively.
    //
    //    request.queryParams may be undefined (no query string supplied).
    //    request.queryParams.number may be undefined (parameter absent),
    //    a String (single value supplied), or an Array (when the URL has
    //    duplicate parameter names, e.g. ?number=A&number=B - the platform
    //    typically deduplicates but defensive code handles both shapes).
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    var caseNumber = '';
    if (request.queryParams && request.queryParams.number) {
        var raw = request.queryParams.number;
        if (Array.isArray(raw)) {
            // URL had ?number=A&number=B (rare). Take the first value.
            // Returning an error ("multiple values supplied") would leak
            // information about the API's parameter shape; instead,
            // silently honor the first value to maintain the simple
            // 200/404 response surface.
            raw = raw.length > 0 ? raw[0] : '';
        }
        // Coerce-to-String defensively (raw may arrive as Number on some
        // platform versions when the query value is numeric-looking) and
        // trim leading/trailing whitespace.
        caseNumber = String(raw || '').trim();
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2. Empty/missing parameter -> verbatim 404 (information-leakage
    //    hardening). DO NOT differentiate "missing parameter" from "case
    //    not found": returning HTTP 400 with "Missing 'number' parameter"
    //    would tell anonymous callers (potential attackers) the parameter
    //    name and shape, useful for crafting follow-on attacks. Returning
    //    the same 404 response gives no information about the API's
    //    parameter expectations beyond what is already documented in the
    //    public widget code.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (!caseNumber) {
        response.setStatus(404);
        response.setBody({ error: 'No case found with that number.' });
        return;
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3. Delegate to the Script Include. The Script Include is the single
    //    source of truth for:
    //      - The GlideRecord query against x_casemgmt_case
    //      - The field whitelist (returns ONLY status, subject, opened_date)
    //      - The lookup-by-number contract (matches AAP Section 0.7.2's
    //        no-hardcoded-sys_id rule by querying the public 'number' field)
    //
    //    Contract:
    //      - lookupCase(<non-empty trimmed string>) returns:
    //          * null       - no case matches the supplied number
    //          * { status: String, subject: String, opened_date: String }
    //                       - case found, all values pre-coerced to strings
    //
    //    The Script Include is invoked via the scope-qualified API name
    //    `x_casemgmt.CasePortalService` (NOT by sys_id), which complies
    //    with AAP Section 0.7.2's no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    var svc = new x_casemgmt.CasePortalService();
    var result = svc.lookupCase(caseNumber);

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4. No-match -> verbatim 404. Per AAP Section 0.7.4, the literal text
    //    'No case found with that number.' MUST appear in the response.
    //    This is the SAME response shape returned in step 2 for empty/
    //    missing parameters - intentional uniformity prevents anonymous
    //    callers from distinguishing "parameter absent" from "case not found".
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (result === null || result === undefined) {
        response.setStatus(404);
        response.setBody({ error: 'No case found with that number.' });
        return;
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 5. Match -> HTTP 200 with the three whitelisted fields.
    //
    //    The Script Include already coerces to String(...) and applies
    //    `|| ''` defaults; THIS extraction is a defense-in-depth layer
    //    that:
    //      a. Re-coerces in case the Script Include's contract changes
    //         (e.g., a future refactor accidentally returns GlideElement
    //         instances, which would serialize unpredictably).
    //      b. Drops any additional fields the Script Include may return
    //         (defense against accidental field exposure in future edits).
    //      c. Replaces null/undefined with empty string (cleaner JSON
    //         than `null` or the literal text "undefined" for missing
    //         field values).
    //
    //    Response body shape (exactly three keys, no others):
    //      {
    //        status:      "<value or empty string>",
    //        subject:     "<value or empty string>",
    //        opened_date: "<value or empty string>"
    //      }
    //
    //    Internal fields that MUST NOT appear in this response (per AAP
    //    Section 0.4.4):
    //      assigned_group, assigned_agent, description, closed_date,
    //      requester_name, requester_email, priority, type, pending_reason,
    //      sys_id, sys_created_by, sys_created_on, sys_updated_by,
    //      sys_updated_on, sys_mod_count, sys_class_name, sys_domain.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    response.setStatus(200);
    response.setBody({
        status:      String(result.status      || ''),
        subject:     String(result.subject     || ''),
        opened_date: String(result.opened_date || '')
    });
})(request, response);</operation_script>

The success callback * mutates c.data.confirmationWidget.options. * number to pass the auto-generated case * number to the embedded widget. * c.data.submitted - boolean; flipped to * true after a successful POST. Drives * the conditional swap from the form panel * to the embedded confirmation widget panel. * c.data.submittedNumber - string; mirrors * the case number for any consumers that * want it directly off c.data (defense-in- * depth, in case the embedded widget's * options object is replaced rather than * mutated by some future refactor). * * Exposed method (template-bound): * c.submit() - executes the case submission. Please try again." is * hardcoded in this controller via direct assignment to * c.errorMessage. Please * try again." The error message // and submitting flag drive mutually-exclusive UI affordances. c.submitting = true; c.errorMessage = ''; // POST to the scripted REST endpoint. The payload is built by // enumerating EXACTLY the five whitelisted fields - NOT by // passing c.formData wholesale - so any future expansion of // c.formData does not accidentally widen the payload surface. // This is defense-in-depth alongside the server-side whitelist // enforced by x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.submitCase(). $http.post('/api/x_casemgmt/case_submit', { subject: c.formData.subject, type: c.formData.type, description: c.formData.description, requester_name: c.formData.requester_name, requester_email: c.formData.requester_email }).then(function(response) { // Success path (HTTP 2xx). Renders a 5-field form (subject, type, description, requester_name, requester_email) and POSTs to /api/x_casemgmt/case_submit on Submit. On success, embeds the confirmation widget (sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget) via $sp.getWidget() and the <sp-widget> directive, passing the auto-generated case number through c.data.confirmationWidget.options.number so the embedded widget renders the verbatim message 'Your case has been submitted' plus the case number per AAP Section 0.4.4. Replaces ArkCase's acm-service-portal-gateway DefaultPluggablePortalRequestService.submitRequest pattern. No client-side or server-side database operations - all writes flow through the scripted REST endpoint. On * any error (HTTP 4xx/5xx, network), sets * c.notFound = true so the verbatim message is * rendered. * * Design rationale: * - controller-as syntax (`var c = this`) per AAP Section 0.5.1's * widget-authoring conventions and per the sibling confirmation * widget at ./sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget.xml. * - $http (NOT fetch): Service Portal widgets run in AngularJS * 1.5.x context; $http is the canonical HTTP client. fetch() * would bypass AngularJS's digest cycle and require manual * $scope.$apply() handling. * - encodeURIComponent on the case number: defensive URL escaping. * Even though normal case numbers (CASE0000001) contain no * special characters, defensive encoding prevents URL-injection * attacks if a malicious user submits a crafted string. * - Strict 3-field whitelist on response.data: defense-in-depth. * Even if the server's response somehow contained additional * fields (e.g., due to a future refactor of the Script Include), * this client controller extracts ONLY status/subject/opened_date * so no internal data leaks to the template. * - Verbatim error message in template, NOT echoed from server: * the message "No case found with that number." (AAP Section * 0.7.4) is hardcoded in the template via ng-if="c.notFound". * This controller deliberately does NOT pass error.data.error * or error.statusText to the template - the server's error * body is NEVER trusted by the client. * - Identical handling of all HTTP errors: information-leakage * hardening. 404 (not-found), 500 (server-error), 400 (bad- * request), and 0 (network-error) all set c.notFound = true. * An attacker cannot distinguish "case not found" from "API * down" from any other failure mode. * - c.loading flag: prevents double-lookup race conditions if * the user clicks the button twice quickly, AND drives the * "Looking up..." button text for clear UX feedback. */ var c = this; // Lookup state. Initialize with safe defaults so the template's // ng-if expressions evaluate cleanly even before c.lookup() runs. c.caseNumber = ''; c.result = null; c.notFound = false; c.loading = false; /** * Look up the status of a case by its number via the scripted REST * endpoint at /api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup. * * Per AAP Section 0.4.4: returns ONLY status, subject, opened_date * via strict 3-field whitelist on the response. * * Per AAP Section 0.7.4: on no-match (HTTP 404 or any other error), * the verbatim text "No case found with that number." is rendered * by the template. This function MUST NOT echo error.data.error or * any server-supplied text. */ c.lookup = function() { // Idempotent guard: prevent double-lookup if the user clicks // the button or presses Enter while a request is in flight. if (c.loading) { return; } // Empty-input guard: do not issue a request if the case number // is empty or whitespace-only. The button is also disabled in // this case via ng-disabled, but the guard provides defense- // in-depth in case the disabled state is bypassed (e.g., by // pressing Enter in some edge browsers). if (!c.caseNumber || String(c.caseNumber).trim() === '') { return; } // Reset state at the start of every lookup. The result panel // and the not-found panel are mutually exclusive: only one of // c.result and c.notFound can be truthy at any time. c.loading = true; c.result = null; c.notFound = false; // Build the URL with defensive URL-encoding of the case number. // The server-side Script Include x_casemgmt.CasePortalService. // lookupCase() trims whitespace and queries by the case 'number' // field. encodeURIComponent() handles any whitespace, special // characters, or potentially malicious input safely. var url = '/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup?number=' + encodeURIComponent(String(c.caseNumber).trim()); $http.get(url).then(function(response) { // Success path (HTTP 200). The server's REST operation // returns { status, subject, opened_date } per its contract. c.loading = false; if (response && response.data) { // Strict 3-field whitelist (defense-in-depth). Extract // ONLY status, subject, opened_date from the response // body. Even if the server were misconfigured to return // additional fields, this widget would not display them. // String() coercion handles undefined/null gracefully - // the template renders an empty cell rather than the // literal text "undefined" or "null". c.result = { status: String(response.data.status || ''), subject: String(response.data.subject || ''), opened_date: String(response.data.opened_date || '') }; c.notFound = false; } else { // Defensive: empty response body but HTTP 200. Treat as // not-found rather than rendering an empty result panel. // This should not occur in practice (the server always // returns a body on 200) but guards against unexpected // upstream behavior. c.result = null; c.notFound = true; } }, function(error) { // Error path (HTTP 4xx, 5xx, or network failure / 0). // ALL error types are treated identically per the // information-leakage hardening discussed in the file // header comment. The verbatim text "No case found with // that number." (AAP Section 0.7.4) is rendered by the // template; this function MUST NOT echo error.data.error, // error.statusText, or any server-supplied content. c.loading = false; c.result = null; c.notFound = true; }); }; } ]]> c sp_instance Custom unauthenticated Service Portal widget for case status lookup. Renders a single case-number input field plus a Look Up Status button, GETs /api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup, and displays ONLY the whitelisted fields { status, subject, opened_date } on match or the verbatim text 'No case found with that number.' on no-match per AAP Section 0.7.4. Embedded by sp_page_x_casemgmt_case_status. No internal fields (assigned_group, assigned_agent, description, closed_date, requester_name, requester_email, priority, type, pending_reason, audit fields) are exposed. All HTTP errors (404, 500, 400, network) render the same verbatim message for information-leakage hardening. Replaces ArkCase's GetCaseByNumberServiceImpl.getCaseByNumber() and PortalRequestService.getRequestStatus() Spring services. No client-side or server-side database operations - all data flows through the scripted REST endpoint. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 0.5.1, and 0.7.4 (verbatim no-case-found message) and Validation Gate 5 (Portal - lookup). false x_casemgmt_case_lookup_widget false Case Lookup Widget [] false true false sp_widget admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 e992deb0bd1657f36a38f5af6a46aeb2 0 Case Lookup Widget x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_lookup_widget admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00
