sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script_fix"> <sys_script_fix action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <before>false</before> <description>Post-import remediation for the x_casemgmt scoped application. Completes the four pieces of wiring an Update Set commit cannot perform for itself, because each is produced by a platform business rule and the commit engine applies payloads with business rules suppressed: Defect C (physical case_task/case_party tables, their fields and all seven choice lists - DDL comes from the after-insert business rule 'Synch Dictionary and Table' on sys_db_object); Defect E (auto-number default_value javascript:global.getNextObjNumberPadded(); on x_casemgmt_case.number plus maximum_digits=7 on the counters); Defect 7 (service_id on the two sys_ws_definition records); Defect 9 (the 27 sys_security_acl_role links plus a GlideSecurityManager security-cache flush). Body is scripts/post_import_remediation.js verbatim. IMPORTANT - RUNNING THIS INSTALLED RECORD CANNOT COMPLETE C OR 9. The package declares this record sys_scope=global, but the Update Set commit engine rewrites every committed record's sys_scope to the application, so after commit this Fix Script is x_casemgmt-scoped and its GlideTableDescriptor/GlideSecurityManager calls are refused. Measured outcome of running it from the Fix Script UI: verified=false, tables_built=0, acl_links_created=0, errors=121, every error being one of those two SecurityExceptions. No packaging change fixes this because the rewrite happens at commit time. THE ROUTE THAT WORKS: paste scripts/post_import_remediation.js into System Definition > Scripts - Background with 'In scope' = Global and run it - see docs/HUMAN_DEPLOYMENT_RECREATE_GUIDE.md section 5, acceptance path (b), and docs/PDI_LIMITATIONS_AND_KNOWN_ISSUES.md section 9.4 for the evidence. A companion after-update Business Rule ('x_casemgmt Post-Import Bootstrap' on sys_remote_update_set) that dispatched this Fix Script on commit was built, measured firing and then failing for the same reason, and has been REMOVED from the package: besides being unable to succeed, its condition fired on the commit of ANY retrieved Update Set rather than only this application's, so activating it would have dispatched this privileged, partly destructive remediation on unrelated deployments. The disclosed manual route above replaces it. This script still deactivates a legacy copy of that rule if one is installed, identified by name AND collection AND sys_update_name with exactly one match required. Idempotent and semantically convergent: every insert is lookup-guarded, every dictionary and choice attribute is compared against the package and repaired, the exact 7-list/24-value choice set is verified, and the ACL-to-role wiring is verified as an exact 27-pair set with unexpected pairs removed. The table rebuild is fail-closed: a tri-state physical-storage probe over three independent signals, no deletion unless all three agree there is no storage, and every deletion verified and read back. Emits gs.info lines prefixed X_CASEMGMT_REMEDIATION| and a final SUMMARY| line carrying verified=true|false.</description> <name>x_casemgmt Post-Import Remediation</name> <record_for_rollback>true</record_for_rollback> <script><![CDATA[/* * x_casemgmt_case_management - Post-Import Remediation Script * * Idempotent server-side script that completes the four remediations a * ServiceNow Update Set commit cannot perform for itself. * * THIS IS A REQUIRED POST-IMPORT STEP, NOT AN AUTOMATIC ONE. Importing * update-set/x_casemgmt_case_management_update_set.xml previews and commits * cleanly, but the commit alone does NOT yield a functional application: * Defect C (physical tables/fields/choices) and Defect 9 (the 27 ACL -> role * links) still need this script, and it must be executed BY HAND in the * **Global** scope. The packaged auto-execute trigger was measured firing and * then failing - see "HOW IT IS INVOKED" below and * ../docs/PDI_LIMITATIONS_AND_KNOWN_ISSUES.md section 9.4 - so the acceptance * path for this deliverable is the disclosed manual path (b), and * ../docs/HUMAN_DEPLOYMENT_RECREATE_GUIDE.md section 5 is the procedure that * actually works. Defects E and 7 need no script at all: they are carried by * the package artifacts, and this script only re-asserts them. * * --------------------------------------------------------------------------- * WHAT THIS SCRIPT FIXES, AND WHY THE UPDATE SET CANNOT DO IT ALONE * --------------------------------------------------------------------------- * The Update Set commit engine (GlideUpdateManager2) applies every captured * payload with the target record's *business rules suppressed*. Four pieces of * this application's wiring are produced by platform business rules rather than * by record data, so committing the metadata is necessary but not sufficient. * Each of the four was root-caused empirically on the target PDI: * * Defect C - physical tables, fields and choice lists. * The physical DDL for a brand-new table is executed by the platform's * after-insert business rule `Synch Dictionary and Table` (order 500) on * `sys_db_object`. Applying a `sys_db_object` payload through the engine * inserts the metadata row and stops there: no `sys_dictionary` * collection row, no columns, no physical table. Adding a collection row * to the payload does NOT substitute for the business rule (verified). * A fresh GlideRecord INSERT with workflow ON does run it. * * Defect E - auto-numbering. * Two independent gaps: (a) the `number` dictionary entry needs * `default_value = javascript:global.getNextObjNumberPadded();` - the * `global.` qualifier is mandatory because the caller is a scoped table; * (b) the counter needs `maximum_digits = 7` so the generated value is * CASE0000001 rather than CASE1. Both values are now carried by the * package (dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_number.xml and * numbers/sys_number_x_casemgmt_case*.xml), so on a clean import this * section is a no-op verification pass. It still runs, because Defect C's * table rebuild re-creates the `number` dictionary entry from scratch and * the platform's `Create Default Number Maintenance Field` business rule * - which would normally wire it - is itself suppressed on commit. * * Defect 7 - scripted REST routing. * `sys_ws_definition.service_id` is the URL path segment. The package now * carries both values, so on a clean import this section is a no-op * verification pass; it remains here so a partially-repaired instance * converges. * * Defect 9 - ACL -> role link records. * On a high-security instance an ACL with no role, no condition and no * script evaluates to DENY ("Deny access for empty term"), so an * application whose 26 ACLs carry no role links is unusable by every * non-admin. `sys_security_acl` has no `roles` column on this release * (confirmed against sys_dictionary for the table and its sys_metadata * super-class), so the `<roles>` element every ACL artifact carries is * ignored when the record is written: the links live only in the * `sys_security_acl_role` m2m table. Payloads for that table are silently * skipped by the update engine (verified against five payload shapes, * including the platform's own serialization), so creating the links from * this script is the only route that works. The roles themselves are not * invented: the engine keeps each ACL's incoming payload as a * `sys_update_version` row, so the package's own `<roles>` declaration is * read back from there by name - see rolesFromCommittedPayload(). * Enforcement additionally requires a security-cache flush, which is * performed here rather than asked of an operator. * * --------------------------------------------------------------------------- * EXECUTION SCOPE - READ THIS BEFORE RUNNING * --------------------------------------------------------------------------- * EVERY section of this script must run in the **global** scope. * * - `sys_db_object`, `sys_dictionary`, `sys_choice`, `sys_number`, * `sys_ws_definition`, `sys_security_acl`, `sys_security_acl_role` and * `sys_script` all live in the global scope with cross-scope * create/update access denied, so a scoped caller cannot write any of them. * - `GlideTableDescriptor` raises * "GlideTableDescriptor is not allowed in scoped applications" when the * caller is scoped, so the physical-table checks only work from global. * - `GlideSecurityManager` is likewise unavailable to a scoped caller. * * This script therefore writes NO `x_casemgmt_*` data rows at all - seeding * demo data is the separate, in-scope job of ./seed_demo_data.js. The two * scripts are complementary and are run in different scopes: * * post_import_remediation.js -> global * seed_demo_data.js -> x_casemgmt (scope sys_id) * * HOW IT IS INVOKED - THE ONE ROUTE THAT WAS MEASURED TO WORK * Paste this file into **System Definition -> Scripts - Background** with * **"In scope" = Global** and run it. That is the only invocation route proven * on the target PDI, and it is step 4 (and again step 6) of * ../docs/HUMAN_DEPLOYMENT_RECREATE_GUIDE.md section 5. * * ONE other copy of this body ships inside the package. It cannot perform * Defect C or Defect 9, and it is shipped for disclosure and for reuse on an * instance where the scope rewrite below does not apply - not as a working * fallback: * * a. scripts/sys_script_fix_x_casemgmt_post_import_remediation.xml - a Fix * Script named "x_casemgmt Post-Import Remediation" whose `script` field is * this file verbatim, byte for byte. The package declares it * `sys_scope = global`, but **the Update Set commit engine rewrites every * committed record's `sys_scope` to the Update Set's application**: read * back after commit, the installed Fix Script is app-scoped. Running it * from the Fix Script UI therefore executes in `x_casemgmt`, where * `GlideTableDescriptor` and `GlideSecurityManager` are refused. Measured * outcome: `verified=false`, `tables_built=0`, `acl_links_created=0`, * `errors=121`, all 121 being those two SecurityExceptions. * * AN AUTO-EXECUTE TRIGGER WAS BUILT AND HAS BEEN REMOVED. An earlier revision * also shipped a sys_script_x_casemgmt_post_import_bootstrap.xml artifact - a * global after-update Business Rule on `sys_remote_update_set`, condition * `current.state.changesTo('committed')`, which resolved the Fix Script by name * and dispatched it with `GlideScopedEvaluator`. It was measured FIRING * correctly on commit and then failing for exactly the reason in (a), so it was * shipped inactive. It is now gone from the package altogether, for a second and * independent reason: its condition matched the commit of ANY retrieved Update * Set, not only this application's, so activating it - or an instance carrying * an earlier active copy - would dispatch this privileged, partly destructive * remediation on unrelated deployments. deactivateBootstrapTrigger() below * therefore exists to QUIET such a legacy copy, identified by name AND * `collection` AND `sys_update_name` with exactly one match required. * * The full evidence, including the verbatim syslog lines, is in * ../docs/PDI_LIMITATIONS_AND_KNOWN_ISSUES.md section 9.4. * * VERIFICATION SIGNAL (what to look for to prove it ran) * Every line this script emits is a `gs.info()` prefixed with the grep-able * marker `X_CASEMGMT_REMEDIATION|`. Read them back with: * System Logs -> All -> Message starts with X_CASEMGMT_REMEDIATION * or: * GET /api/now/table/syslog * ?sysparm_query=messageSTARTSWITHX_CASEMGMT_REMEDIATION * &sysparm_fields=sys_created_on,message&sysparm_limit=100 * The final line is the single summary line and always starts with * `X_CASEMGMT_REMEDIATION|SUMMARY|`. Its presence is the proof the script * ran to completion; its `verified=` token is the proof the remediation * converged. * * IDEMPOTENCY AND CONVERGENCE GUARANTEES * - Every insert is preceded by a lookup, and every write is preceded by a * comparison against the authoritative specification below. * - Convergence is SEMANTIC, not merely existential. The physical column * existing is not treated as proof the field is correct: every attribute the * package declares (type, length, choice, mandatory, read-only, display, * unique, default sort, reference target, default value, active) is compared * against the stored `sys_dictionary` row and repaired where it differs, and * every choice row's label, sequence, inactive flag and language are * compared and repaired the same way. Verification then re-reads all of it * from the database, plus the exact choice-value set and the exact * ACL -> role pair set, so a malformed schema cannot report `verified=true`. * - A second run therefore creates nothing, changes nothing, and emits only * "already correct" traces plus the summary line. Both runs report the same * `verified=true`. * * DESTRUCTIVE-SAFETY GUARANTEES (the rebuild in ensureTable) * - MUTUAL EXCLUSION. The run takes a cluster-wide lease * ('x_casemgmt_post_import_remediation', backed by the platform's own * sys_mutex, the same mechanism the platform uses for NUMBER_MANAGER_* and * AutomatedTestingFrameworkMutex:*) BEFORE the first probe and before any * write, and releases it in a `finally`. If another run holds it, this one * REFUSES immediately, names the holding node and the acquisition time, and * probes and writes nothing - it does not queue behind it, because a silent * 14-second spin-wait (measured) is not what an operator investigating a * stuck run should get. The lease is re-asserted immediately before each of * the two metadata purges, so a lease reaped or released underneath a run * stops the rebuild instead of letting two runs interleave a purge and a * re-insert. * - The rebuild deletes metadata rows, so it is fail-CLOSED on uncertainty. * probePhysicalState() is tri-state: it interrogates three independent * platform signals (`GlideTableDescriptor.isValid`, `GlideRecord.isValid`, * `TableUtils.tableExists`) and returns * 'yes' when ANY signal reports storage - the table is left untouched; * 'no' only when ALL THREE agree there is none - proven metadata-only; * 'unknown' when any signal throws or the signals disagree. * A transient failure, a permission refusal or an API change therefore * produces 'unknown', and 'unknown' ABORTS the table with an error. It never * reaches the delete. The pre-refine version converted any exception to * "not physical" and deleted on that basis; that fail-open path is gone. * - Every deletion is verified: `deleteRecord()`'s return value is checked, the * collection is re-read afterwards, and any residue or any refused delete * aborts the rebuild before the fresh insert. Counters record only verified * removals. * - OWNERSHIP-AWARE SECURITY RECONCILIATION. `sys_security_acl_role` is the * table that grants an operation to a role, so a surplus row is an * over-privileged grant - but it may equally be a deliberate administrator * decision, a grant belonging to a newer version of this application, or * another automation's work. Every surplus row is REPORTED, which makes the * run report verified=false; only a row this installer demonstrably created * is deleted (installerOwnsLink: this application's ACL and role, this * application's scope, and the row's PRIMARY KEY equal to the deterministic * identity installerLinkSysId() stamps on insert - `sys_name` cannot serve as * the marker because the platform rewrites it for everybody). Nothing else is * destroyed on the strength of being unexpected. * - APPLICATION CONFINEMENT. Every privileged lookup is anchored to this * application, never to a display name alone: the scripted REST definitions * are resolved by name AND sys_scope AND sys_package with exactly one match * required (this instance carries several same-named definitions in other * scopes), and a legacy bootstrap Business Rule is only ever modified when * its name, its `collection` and its `sys_update_name` all match this * package's own payload and exactly one row does. A near-miss is reported and * left alone rather than modified. * * CONSTRAINTS HONORED * - Zero hard-coded foreign sys_ids. The application scope is resolved by * name (`sys_scope.scope = 'x_casemgmt'`), roles by `sys_user_role.name`, * tables by `sys_db_object.name`, dictionary entries by * (`name`, `element`), choices by (`name`, `element`, `value`), counters by * `sys_number.category`, REST definitions by `sys_ws_definition.name` within * this application's `sys_scope`, and ACLs by their own `name` + * `description`. When a table has to be rebuilt, * its existing sys_id is read from the database and re-used so every * reference in the package stays valid. The ACL -> role pair set is keyed on * sys_ids too, but both sides are read out of the database in the same run. * There is not one 32-character hex literal in this file. * - Zero PII and zero synthetic data creation: this script only repairs * metadata and security wiring. It creates no users, groups or cases. * - No email: no gs.eventQueue(), no notification dispatch. * - No `gs.print()` (forbidden in scoped contexts and useless inside a * business rule) - all output goes through gs.info()/gs.warn(). * - No `gs.nowDateTime()` (scope-fenced on this release) - `new * GlideDateTime()` is used instead. * - `case` is a JavaScript reserved word: the case_task/case_party reference * field named `case` is only ever handled as the string 'case' and read * with getValue('case'), never as a property accessor. * - ES5 only - no arrow functions, no const/let, no template literals, no * destructuring - so the file runs unchanged on Rhino-based releases. * * AUTHORITATIVE SPECIFICATION * Table, field and choice definitions below are transcribed from the * package's own artifacts (../tables/*.xml, ../dictionary/*.xml, * ../choices/*.xml) which in turn mirror ../docs/data-model.md verbatim. * Nothing here is invented; this script rebuilds only what the deliverable * already declares. * * SOURCE-SIDE SEMANTIC REFERENCES (read-only context; no ArkCase code reused) * acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/.../CaseFile.java * acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-task-plugin/.../AcmTask.java * acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-person-plugin/.../PersonAssociation.java * acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-admin-plugin/.../RolesPrivilegesService.java */
/* global GlideRecord, GlideAggregate, GlideDateTime, GlideTableDescriptor, GlideSecurityManager, GlideMutex, TableUtils, gs */ /* eslint-env es5 */
// ============================================================================ // Constants // ============================================================================
// Grep-able marker prefixed to every log line this script emits. Searching // syslog for `LOG_MARKER + '|SUMMARY|'` is how an operator confirms the // remediation ran, and its `verified=` token is how they confirm it converged. var LOG_MARKER = 'X_CASEMGMT_REMEDIATION';
// The scoped application's namespace. Used to resolve the scope record by name // (never by sys_id) and to select this application's ACLs. var SCOPE_NAME = 'x_casemgmt';
// The three scoped tables, in dependency order: x_casemgmt_case must exist // before case_task/case_party, because both carry a reference field to it. var TABLE_CASE = 'x_casemgmt_case'; var TABLE_CASE_TASK = 'x_casemgmt_case_task'; var TABLE_CASE_PARTY = 'x_casemgmt_case_party';
// The three scoped roles, resolved by name at run time. var ROLE_MANAGER = 'x_casemgmt_case_manager'; var ROLE_AGENT = 'x_casemgmt_case_agent'; var ROLE_VIEWER = 'x_casemgmt_case_viewer';
// The number of ACL -> role link records the package requires: 26 ACLs, of which // the `assigned_agent` field ACL needs two roles (manager AND the assigned // agent), so 25 x 1 + 1 x 2 = 27. This is an invariant, not a target to grow // into: a run that produces fewer links has failed to derive a mapping and is // reported as not converged rather than quietly shipping a partly-open // application. See rolesForAcl() for how each link is derived. var EXPECTED_ACL_ROLE_LINKS = 27; var EXPECTED_ACL_COUNT = 26;
// How those 27 links distribute across the three roles. Derived by reading the // `<roles>` element of all 26 ../acl/*.xml artifacts: the manager appears on // every table-level operation of all three tables (12) plus both field ACLs (2); // the agent on create/read/write of all three tables (9) plus the assigned_agent // field ACL (1); the viewer on read of all three tables (3). // // This is a fail-closed cross-check on the DERIVATION, not just on the total: if // rolesForAcl() ever mapped an ACL to the wrong role the total could still be 27 // while the distribution moved, so both are asserted. var EXPECTED_ROLE_LINK_COUNTS = { 'x_casemgmt_case_manager': 14, 'x_casemgmt_case_agent': 10, 'x_casemgmt_case_viewer': 3 };
// Name of the bootstrap Business Rule that WAS built to auto-execute this script // and has been REMOVED from the package (see the header) - kept here only so // deactivateBootstrapTrigger() can recognise a legacy copy - and of the Fix Script // that carries this body. Both are looked up by name, so this file carries no // sys_id for either. // // IMPORTANT: `sys_script.name` and `sys_script_fix.name` are both max_length 40 // on this release and the platform truncates silently. A longer name would still // import, but every name-based lookup - including deactivateBootstrapTrigger() // below - would then fail to match. Keep both names at 40 characters or fewer. var BOOTSTRAP_TRIGGER_NAME = 'x_casemgmt Post-Import Bootstrap'; var FIX_SCRIPT_NAME = 'x_casemgmt Post-Import Remediation';
// The table and update name that a legacy copy of the bootstrap trigger MUST // carry before this script is willing to touch it. The package no longer ships // that trigger at all (see the header), so deactivateBootstrapTrigger() exists // only to quiet a copy left behind by an earlier version of this package - and a // name alone is not enough to identify one: another application is free to own a // Business Rule with the same name. All three of these must match, and exactly // one row may match, or nothing is touched. var BOOTSTRAP_TRIGGER_TABLE = 'sys_remote_update_set'; var BOOTSTRAP_TRIGGER_UPDATE_NAME = 'sys_script_x_casemgmt_post_import_bootstrap';

// ---- Defect C: physical tables, fields, choice lists -------------------- var i; var j; for (i = 0; i < TABLE_SPECS.length; i++) { ensureTable(TABLE_SPECS[i], scopeSysId); } // Runs whether or not ensureTable() had to build anything: a table the // commit created successfully still carries the committed access flags, and // those decide both whether a cross-scope read is refused and whether a // cross-scope WRITE is permitted (see TABLE_ACCESS_SPEC). for (i = 0; i < TABLE_SPECS.length; i++) { ensureTableAccess(TABLE_SPECS[i]); } for (i = 0; i < TABLE_SPECS.length; i++) { for (j = 0; j < TABLE_SPECS[i].fields.length; j++) { ensureField(TABLE_SPECS[i].name, TABLE_SPECS[i].fields[j], scopeSysId); } } // After the fields, not during them: the platform clears every other column's // display flag when one is set, so the single-display-field invariant is // asserted once per table at the end rather than field by field. for (i = 0; i < TABLE_SPECS.length; i++) { ensureSingleDisplayField(TABLE_SPECS[i]); } for (i = 0; i < CHOICE_SPECS.length; i++) { ensureChoice(CHOICE_SPECS[i], scopeSysId); } log('DEFECT_C|tables_built=' + STATS.tablesBuilt + '|tables_already_physical=' + STATS.tablesAlready + '|tables_indeterminate=' + STATS.tablesUncertain + '|cross_scope_access_repaired=' + STATS.tableAccessRepaired + '|cross_scope_access_already_correct=' + STATS.tableAccessAlready + '|fields_created=' + STATS.fieldsCreated + '|fields_repaired=' + STATS.fieldsRepaired + '|fields_already_correct=' + STATS.fieldsAlready + '|display_fields_reconciled=' + STATS.displayFieldsFixed + '|choices_created=' + STATS.choicesCreated + '|choices_repaired=' + STATS.choicesRepaired + '|choices_already_correct=' + STATS.choicesAlready);
// ---- Defect E: auto-numbering ------------------------------------------ for (i = 0; i < COUNTER_SPECS.length; i++) { ensureCounter(COUNTER_SPECS[i], scopeSysId); } ensureNumberDefault(TABLE_CASE); verifyNumberDefaultIsLive(); log('DEFECT_E|counters_written=' + STATS.countersUpdated + '|counters_already_correct=' + STATS.countersAlready + '|number_defaults_written=' + STATS.numberDefaultsSet + '|number_defaults_already_correct=' + STATS.numberDefaultsAlready);
// ---- Defect 7: scripted REST routing ----------------------------------- for (i = 0; i < REST_SPECS.length; i++) { ensureServiceId(REST_SPECS[i], scopeSysId); } log('DEFECT_7|service_ids_written=' + STATS.serviceIdsSet + '|service_ids_already_correct=' + STATS.serviceIdsAlready);
// ---- Defect 9: ACL role links + security cache flush ------------------- var links = ensureAllAclRoleLinks(scopeSysId); var linkTotal = links.total; flushSecurityCache(); log('DEFECT_9|links_created=' + STATS.aclLinksCreated + '|links_already_present=' + STATS.aclLinksAlready + '|installer_owned_links_removed=' + STATS.aclLinksRemoved + '|foreign_links_reported_not_removed=' + STATS.aclLinksReported + '|links_total=' + linkTotal + '|links_expected=' + EXPECTED_ACL_ROLE_LINKS + '|links_by_role=' + describeCounts(links.byRole) + '|unexpected_links=' + links.extras.length + '|missing_links=' + links.missing.length + '|unmapped_acls=' + STATS.aclsUnmapped + '|security_cache_flushed=' + (STATS.securityCacheFlushes > 0));
// ---- Verification ------------------------------------------------------ var result = verifyRemediation(scopeSysId); log('VERIFY|' + result.detail); if (!result.ok) { for (i = 0; i < result.problems.length; i++) { logError('VERIFY|unresolved: ' + result.problems[i]); } } else { deactivateBootstrapTrigger(); }
var finished = new GlideDateTime(); var summary = 'SUMMARY|verified=' + result.ok + '|tables_built=' + STATS.tablesBuilt + '|tables_already=' + STATS.tablesAlready + '|tables_indeterminate=' + STATS.tablesUncertain + '|fields_created=' + STATS.fieldsCreated + '|fields_repaired=' + STATS.fieldsRepaired + '|fields_already=' + STATS.fieldsAlready + '|display_reconciled=' + STATS.displayFieldsFixed + '|choices_created=' + STATS.choicesCreated + '|choices_repaired=' + STATS.choicesRepaired + '|choices_already=' + STATS.choicesAlready + '|counters_written=' + STATS.countersUpdated + '|counters_already=' + STATS.countersAlready + '|number_default_written=' + STATS.numberDefaultsSet + '|number_default_already=' + STATS.numberDefaultsAlready + '|service_ids_written=' + STATS.serviceIdsSet + '|service_ids_already=' + STATS.serviceIdsAlready + '|acl_links_created=' + STATS.aclLinksCreated + '|acl_links_already=' + STATS.aclLinksAlready + '|acl_links_removed_mine=' + STATS.aclLinksRemoved + '|acl_links_reported_not_mine=' + STATS.aclLinksReported + '|acl_links_total=' + linkTotal + '|acl_links_expected=' + EXPECTED_ACL_ROLE_LINKS + '|security_cache_flushed=' + (STATS.securityCacheFlushes > 0) + '|lease=' + LEASE_NAME + '|lease_held_during_run=' + (LEASE.acquiredAt || 'no') + '|errors=' + STATS.errors + '|finished=' + finished.getDisplayValue(); log(summary); return summary; }
// ============================================================================ // Auto-execution // ============================================================================ // // Calling the entry point from the bottom of the file keeps it drop-in runnable // with no extra boilerplate in the one route that was measured to work - // System Definition -> Scripts - Background with "In scope" = Global - and in the // two packaged copies, which run the same body but are forced into the // application scope by the commit engine and therefore cannot complete (see // "HOW IT IS INVOKED" in the header). // // The call is safe to repeat: see the idempotency and convergence guarantees in // the header.
postImportRemediation(); ]]></script> <sys_class_name>sys_script_fix</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>227b757f182d8f3e1d9b774187ae8358</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>x_casemgmt Post-Import Remediation</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Global" source="global">global</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Global">global</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>sys_script_fix_x_casemgmt_post_import_remediation</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <unloadable>false</unloadable> </sys_script_fix> </record_update>

This is the row that appears in the Performance Analytics dashboard catalog under the title "Agent Workspace" with description shown in the catalog tooltip.

Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_my_open_cases.xml report (type=list) showing the cases assigned to the current user where status NOT IN (Resolved, Closed). Per the underlying report's filter, this is "the agent's daily-driver list" - the rows the agent will work on today.
Position math (12-column grid): column=1, width=6 -> occupies columns 1-6 row=1, height=4 -> occupies rows 1-4
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "MY work-in-flight" view that an agent reaches for FIRST when opening their dashboard. Top-left is the natural eye-scan starting point on any LTR-language dashboard. Per Validation Gate 6, this widget MUST render with at least 1 row from x_casemgmt_case where assigned_agent = the demo agent's sys_id AND status NOT IN (Resolved, Closed). Per AAP Section 0.4.1, demo cases 02, 03, 04, 07, 08 are in {Open, In Progress, Pending} statuses; the demo agent MUST be assigned_agent on at least one of these (the seed-data agent ensures this).
Why a list widget (not a chart): per AAP Section 0.4.4, the agent needs ROW-LEVEL detail to click into individual cases. A donut/bar would obscure case-level access. The list widget renders each row clickable, navigating to the case form on click - matching ArkCase's "case list -> case detail" UX flow.

Per the underlying report's filter, this is "the agent's overdue work" - tasks that have slipped past their deadline and need immediate action.
Position math (12-column grid): column=7, width=6 -> occupies columns 7-12 row=1, height=4 -> occupies rows 1-4
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "fire-fighting view" that an agent reaches for SECOND. Whereas Widget 1 shows all assigned cases regardless of urgency, Widget 2 surfaces tasks (which are more granular than cases) that are explicitly overdue. Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file. - <tab>: record [3] in this file. - <report>: ../reports/x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks</name> and <title>My Overdue Tasks</title>). --> <pa_dashboard_widgets action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <column>7</column> <dashboard display_value="Agent Workspace">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace</dashboard> <height>4</height> <name>x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_my_overdue_tasks</name> <order>20</order> <report display_value="My Overdue Tasks">x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks</report> <row>1</row> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_widgets</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>6c5338b94cdba04e62914586f4e12057</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>My Overdue Tasks</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_widgets_x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_my_overdue_tasks</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <tab display_value="Overview">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_tab_main</tab> <title>My Overdue Tasks</title> <type>report</type> <width>6</width> </pa_dashboard_widgets>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [7] - WIDGET 3: CASE COUNT BY STATUS (DONUT/PIE CHART) =================================================================== The full-width donut chart on row 2. Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status.xml report (type=pie) showing the count of all cases (across the entire team, not just the current agent) grouped by status. The six slices correspond to the six values of x_casemgmt_case.status: Draft, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved, Closed.
Position math (12-column grid): column=1, width=12 -> occupies columns 1-12 (full row) row=5, height=4 -> occupies rows 5-8
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "team-wide context" view that gives the agent perspective on how their work fits into the broader case distribution. While Widgets 1 and 2 are PERSONAL (filter by current user), Widget 3 is GLOBAL (no current-user filter). It deliberately spans the full width of the row because donut chart legibility benefits from horizontal space for slice labels and a horizontal legend.
Why a donut chart (not a bar): per AAP Section 0.4.4, the deliberate diversity of chart types pairs different chart types to different cardinalities - donut is suitable for low-to-medium cardinality (6 buckets here) where the focus is PROPORTIONS. The agent typically wants to see "what fraction of cases are Open vs Closed vs In Progress" rather than absolute counts. Bar would be appropriate for ordered comparison (e.g., priority); donut is appropriate for unordered proportional comparison.
Per Validation Gate 6, this widget MUST render with all six slices populated since AAP Section 0.4.1 mandates seed data spanning all six status values (demo cases 01-10 hit Draft, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved, Closed - one or more per status).
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file. - <tab>: record [3] in this file. - <report>: ../reports/x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status</name> and <title>Case Count by Status</title>). --> <pa_dashboard_widgets action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <column>1</column> <dashboard display_value="Agent Workspace">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace</dashboard> <height>4</height> <name>x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_case_count_by_status</name> <order>30</order> <report display_value="Case Count by Status">x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status</report> <row>5</row> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_widgets</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>4920c9d42b6499f2fe6b1c833cbda375</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>Case Count by Status</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_widgets_x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_case_count_by_status</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <tab display_value="Overview">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_tab_main</tab> <title>Case Count by Status</title> <type>report</type> <width>12</width> </pa_dashboard_widgets>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [8] - ROLE ATTACHMENT (pa_dashboard_role) - case_agent =================================================================== Binds this dashboard to the x_casemgmt_case_agent scoped role. Per the assigned-folder requirements ("Agent Workspace dashboard MUST be visible to x_casemgmt_case_agent (operationally relevant)"), this is the FIRST of two role attachments for this dashboard.
Visibility outcome (combined with record [9]): - Users WITH x_casemgmt_case_agent role: Dashboard appears in the Performance Analytics dashboard catalog and renders all three widgets. Widget 1 shows cases assigned to this user; Widget 2 shows tasks assigned to this user; Widget 3 shows team-wide status distribution. - Users WITH x_casemgmt_case_manager role (record [9]): Dashboard appears in the catalog. Widgets 1 and 2 may render empty if the manager has no personally-assigned cases or tasks; Widget 3 renders fully (team-wide). Managers use this dashboard primarily to monitor agents, with their detailed KPIs in the Manager View dashboard. - Users WITHOUT either role (including x_casemgmt_case_viewer): Dashboard does NOT appear in the catalog by default. Per the assigned-folder requirements, viewers can be "explicitly granted" access on a per-deployment basis - that's a future enhancement, not part of this POC. - Users with the global `admin` role: The platform's admin-overrides behavior typically allows admins to see all dashboards regardless of role attachment. This is intentional - the user's deployment-step 3 (post-commit verification) requires the admin to see and click into the dashboard to confirm widgets render.
Per AAP Section 0.7.2 ("scoped-namespace-only constraint"), no global ServiceNow roles (admin, itil, etc.) are attached here.
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file (x_casemgmt_agent_workspace). - <role>: ../roles/sys_user_role_x_casemgmt_case_agent.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_case_agent</name>).

AND to x_casemgmt_case_manager (monitoring agents)"), this is the SECOND of two role attachments for this dashboard.

<unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00"> <!-- =================================================================== RECORD [1] - CANVAS PANE (sys_grid_canvas_pane) =================================================================== The layout container for the dashboard. ServiceNow's modern dashboard framework binds each pa_dashboards row to a sys_grid_canvas_pane that defines the responsive grid (12-column) onto which widgets are positioned. The dashboard record (record [2] below) carries a `<canvas_id>` reference back to this pane.
Convention: this canvas pane has no special configuration - the platform renders a default 12-column responsive grid with the widgets positioned by their column/row/width/height. No custom CSS, no custom JavaScript, no theming overrides per AAP Section 0.4.4 ("default Service Portal theme. No custom CSS, no custom branding"). --> <sys_grid_canvas_pane action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <name>x_casemgmt_manager_view_canvas</name> <sys_class_name>sys_grid_canvas_pane</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>041b6707a9ea36b9928d6b380ee5b039</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>x_casemgmt_manager_view_canvas</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>sys_grid_canvas_pane_x_casemgmt_manager_view_canvas</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> </sys_grid_canvas_pane>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [2] - DASHBOARD (pa_dashboards) =================================================================== The Manager View dashboard record itself. This is the row that appears in the Performance Analytics dashboard catalog under the title "Manager View" with description shown in the catalog tooltip.
Field decisions: - <active>true</active>: dashboard is published immediately on Update Set commit per AAP Section 0.4.4 (manager users see "operationally relevant aggregate views on day one"). - <canvas_id>: references record [1] above by name; ServiceNow's Update-Set engine resolves this at apply time. - <description>: AAP-mandated one-sentence summary visible in the catalog. Free of PII per AAP Section 0.7.2. - <icon>fa-line-chart</icon>: FontAwesome glyph for visual distinguishing in the catalog. Decorative only. - <is_homepage>false</is_homepage>: this is a Performance Analytics dashboard, not a homepage. ServiceNow homepages are a different concept (sys_portal/sys_portal_page) intended for the user's landing screen on login. - <name>: machine-readable identifier prefixed with x_casemgmt_ per AAP Section 0.7.2 scope-namespace-exclusivity rule. - <order>200</order>: sorts AFTER the Agent Workspace dashboard (order=100) when both are visible. Reading order: agent dashboard first (daily-driver), manager dashboard second (operational-review). - <title>Manager View</title>: human-readable title shown in the catalog and as the dashboard page header. - <sys_policy/>: empty - no scoped policy override; the scoped-application's own ACLs (../acl/) govern access. --> <pa_dashboards action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <active>true</active> <canvas_id display_value="x_casemgmt_manager_view_canvas">x_casemgmt_manager_view_canvas</canvas_id> <description>Operational KPI dashboard for case managers - shows team-wide case distributions across status, type, and priority, plus throughput KPIs (average time to close, cases opened in last 30 days).</description> <icon>fa-line-chart</icon> <is_homepage>false</is_homepage> <name>x_casemgmt_manager_view</name> <order>200</order> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboards</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>6459b19ef618e53a07735c38fc6a1d5c</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>Manager View</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboards_x_casemgmt_manager_view</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <title>Manager View</title> </pa_dashboards>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [3] - TAB (pa_tab) =================================================================== The single tab that hosts all five widgets. ServiceNow Performance Analytics dashboards use a dashboard->tabs->widgets hierarchy. A dashboard may have multiple tabs (Operational KPIs, Backlog, Throughput, etc.); this Manager View has exactly ONE tab named "Operational KPIs" carrying all 5 widgets per AAP-mandated minimal- change discipline (do not introduce additional tabs not specified).
Field decisions: - <active>true</active>: the tab is rendered on the dashboard. - <name>: machine-readable identifier; matches the sys_update_name pattern. - <order>1</order>: position in the dashboard's tab strip (left-most). With only one tab, this value is symbolic. - <title>Operational KPIs</title>: human-readable label shown on the tab itself and in the dashboard's tab navigation. --> <pa_tab action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <active>true</active> <name>x_casemgmt_manager_view_tab_main</name> <order>1</order> <sys_class_name>pa_tab</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>245b2c0dbb907c31da0c2ad45b574803</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>Operational KPIs</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_tab_x_casemgmt_manager_view_tab_main</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <title>Operational KPIs</title> </pa_tab>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [4] - DASHBOARD-TO-TAB MEMBERSHIP (pa_m2m_dashboard_tabs) =================================================================== ServiceNow's pa_m2m_dashboard_tabs is the many-to-many junction table that wires a pa_dashboards record to one or more pa_tab records. <!-- =================================================================== RECORD [5] - WIDGET 1: ALL CASES BY STATUS (BAR CHART) =================================================================== The first chart widget on row 1 (left-most). Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status.xml report (type=bar) showing the count of cases in each of the six status buckets (Draft, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved, Closed).
Position math (12-column grid): column=1, width=4 -> occupies columns 1-4 row=1, height=4 -> occupies rows 1-4
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "lifecycle-stage view" that shows managers where cases pile up. A top-heavy Open/In Progress distribution signals intake-throughput backlog; a top-heavy Pending distribution signals dependency-blocking; a healthy funnel-shape (Open > In Progress > Resolved > Closed) signals normal flow. Per Validation Gate 6, this widget MUST render with the demo seed data spanning all six statuses (per AAP Section 0.4.1, demo cases 01-10 hit every status).
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file. - <tab>: record [3] in this file. - <report>: ../reports/x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status.xml. sys_id of that report is deeaca81d8626c9c2cc2974716efd08c (verified via md5("x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status")). --> <pa_dashboard_widgets action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <column>1</column> <dashboard display_value="Manager View">x_casemgmt_manager_view</dashboard> <height>4</height> <name>x_casemgmt_manager_view_widget_all_cases_by_status</name> <order>10</order> <report display_value="All Cases by Status">x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status</report> <row>1</row> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_widgets</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>4e5ad436431603d5f7da21d74288d99a</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>All Cases by Status</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_widgets_x_casemgmt_manager_view_widget_all_cases_by_status</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <tab display_value="Operational KPIs">x_casemgmt_manager_view_tab_main</tab> <title>All Cases by Status</title> <type>report</type> <width>4</width> </pa_dashboard_widgets>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [6] - WIDGET 2: ALL CASES BY TYPE (DONUT/PIE CHART) =================================================================== The second chart widget on row 1 (center). Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_type.xml report (type=pie) showing the proportion of cases between General Inquiry and Complaint.
Position math (12-column grid): column=5, width=4 -> occupies columns 5-8 row=1, height=4 -> occupies rows 1-4
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "case-handling-pipeline view" that shows managers the SUBDOMAIN MIX between the two case types. The two case types map 1:1 to the two Flow Designer flows defined in ../flows/general_inquiry_state_machine.xml and ../flows/complaint_state_machine.xml. Managers use the proportion to recognize when one pipeline dominates and may require additional staffing or process attention. Per AAP Section 0.4.1, demo cases 01-06 are General Inquiry and 07-10 are Complaint, so this donut renders with two slices summed to 10.
Why donut not bar: per AAP Section 0.4.4, the deliberate diversity of chart types pairs different chart types to different cardinalities - donut for low-cardinality proportions (2 buckets), bar for higher- cardinality magnitude comparison (4-6 buckets). Do NOT flatten the chart type to "all bar" or "all pie" for consistency.

Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "operational throughput KPI" that shows managers how long the team takes on average to close a case. ServiceNow renders single-score widgets as large eye- catching KPI cards. The 6-column width gives the score room for a readable number plus the title.
AGGREGATION STRATEGY ==================== The underlying report (../reports/x_casemgmt_avg_time_to_close.xml) sets `<aggregation_source>duration_to_close</aggregation_source>`, referencing the Function Field defined in ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_duration_to_close.xml. The Function Field is computed at query time by the platform's database- level function `glidefunction:datediff(closed_date,opened_date)` and is consumable by `sys_report` aggregations. The widget renders a Duration-typed AVG of elapsed time between case opening and closure (e.g., "5 Days 03:42:11"). The Update Set imports without preview errors and Validation Gate 6 ("All widgets display data; no broken report references") passes for all eight dashboard widgets across both dashboards.

Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "intake-volume KPI" that shows managers how many new cases entered the system in the most recent 30-day window. Used to detect intake surges (e.g., a service outage flooding the queue) or to compare to historical baselines. The underlying report uses gs.daysAgoStart(30) which returns midnight of the 30th day prior; the count includes cases opened at or after that timestamp through "now".
Per AAP Section 0.7.3 Gate 6, the underlying report MUST produce a non-zero value for this widget to render meaningfully. This depends on: - At least one demo case whose opened_date is within the last 30 days of expected install time. - Per AAP Section 0.4.1, demo cases SHOULD use recent opened_date values (within 30 days of expected install time) for this widget to display a non-zero number. <unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00">
    <sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <document>sys_atf_step</document>
        <document_key>ad11bc7a90d98cdc599f396b8e200c49</document_key>
        <order />
        <sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>deca2d36e5b6170e0a9f681cc2e4b91e</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "probe",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "cfdc67741a52236340f593d0229635a8",
            "prefix": "ATF-DM-01",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-DM-01 data model probe",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "priority": "Medium"
            }
        }
    ];
    // `status` is deliberately ABSENT from the fixture above. This test asserts
    // that a NEW case defaults to Draft (AAP 0.5.7). Supplying the value here made
    // step 2's Record Validation and the default check in step 3 tautological: they
    // only proved the insert wrote back what the test itself had set. With the key
    // omitted, the only thing that can populate the column is the platform's own
    // configuration of it - the dictionary default plus the choice list - so both
    // checks now observe the platform's default rather than the test's own input.

    // A field value written as "@user:<user_name>" or "@group:<name>" is resolved
    // here, at run time, so no identity sys_id is baked into the test definition.
    function resolveToken(v) {
        if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.charAt(0) !== '@') { return v; }
        var sep = v.indexOf(':');
        var kind = v.substring(1, sep), key = v.substring(sep + 1);
        return kind === 'user' ? userId(key) : groupId(key);
    }
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) { old.setWorkflow(false); old.deleteRecord(); }
    }
    for (var f = 0; f < FIX.length; f++) {
        var gr = new GlideRecord(FIX[f].table);
        gr.initialize();
        gr.setNewGuidValue(FIX[f].sys_id);
        for (var fld in FIX[f].fields) gr.setValue(fld, resolveToken(FIX[f].fields[fld]));
        var newId = gr.insert();
        chk('fixture ' + FIX[f].label + ' created', FIX[f].sys_id, newId);
    }
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('fixture setup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture setup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value>
        <variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable>
    </sys_variable_value>
</unload>

<unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00">
    <sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <document>sys_atf_step</document>
        <document_key>7a030ede995b70701f1fb9cc49e9e8be</document_key>
        <order />
        <sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>4361dd709950d6d31dd07ccd373459ed</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }

    // Every application-defined column on a table, sorted. The collection row
    // (element empty) and the platform's own inherited sys_* columns are excluded,
    // so what is left is exactly what this deliverable declares. Used for SET
    // EQUALITY, which is what makes an UNDECLARED extra field fail the test - a
    // per-field existence loop alone can never notice one.
    function appElements(table) {
        var out = [], d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table);
        d.addNotNullQuery('element');
        d.query();
        while (d.next()) {
            var e = d.getValue('element');
            if (e && e.indexOf('sys_') !== 0) { out.push(e); }
        }
        out.sort();
        return out;
    }

    var CASE_SPEC = [
        ['number','string',40,false,true], ['type','string',40,false,false],
        ['status','string',40,true,false], ['priority','string',40,false,false],
        ['subject','string',255,true,false], ['description','string',4000,true,false],
        ['opened_date','glide_date_time',40,false,true], ['closed_date','glide_date_time',40,false,true],
        ['assigned_group','reference',32,false,false], ['assigned_agent','reference',32,false,false],
        ['requester_name','string',100,true,false], ['requester_email','string',100,false,false],
        ['pending_reason','string',40,false,false]
    ];
    for (var i = 0; i < CASE_SPEC.length; i++) {
        var sp = CASE_SPEC[i], d = dict('x_casemgmt_case', sp[0]);
        chkTrue('x_casemgmt_case.' + sp[0] + ' exists', !!d);
        if (!d) continue;
        chk('x_casemgmt_case.' + sp[0] + ' type', sp[1], d.getValue('internal_type'));
        chk('x_casemgmt_case.' + sp[0] + ' max_length', sp[2], d.getValue('max_length'));
        chk('x_casemgmt_case.' + sp[0] + ' mandatory', sp[3], d.getValue('mandatory') == '1');
        chk('x_casemgmt_case.' + sp[0] + ' read_only', sp[4], d.getValue('read_only') == '1');
    }
    chk('assigned_group reference target', 'sys_user_group', dict('x_casemgmt_case','assigned_group').getValue('reference'));
    chk('assigned_agent reference target', 'sys_user', dict('x_casemgmt_case','assigned_agent').getValue('reference'));
    chk('case.type choices', 'General Inquiry,Complaint', choices('x_casemgmt_case','type').join(','));
    chk('case.status choices', 'Draft,Open,In Progress,Pending,Resolved,Closed', choices('x_casemgmt_case','status').join(','));
    chk('case.priority choices', 'Low,Medium,High,Critical', choices('x_casemgmt_case','priority').join(','));
    chk('case.pending_reason choices', 'Awaiting Info,Awaiting Third Party,Other', choices('x_casemgmt_case','pending_reason').join(','));
    var num = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    chkTrue('fixture case is readable', num.get('cfdc67741a52236340f593d0229635a8'));
    chkTrue('generated number matches the CASE0000001 format', /^CASE[0-9]{7}$/.test(num.getValue('number')));
    var counter = new GlideRecord('sys_number');
    counter.addQuery('category', 'x_casemgmt_case'); counter.setLimit(1); counter.query();
    chkTrue('sys_number counter exists for x_casemgmt_case', counter.next());
    chk('number prefix', 'CASE', counter.getValue('prefix'));
    chk('number maximum_digits', '7', counter.getValue('maximum_digits'));
    // A new case must arrive at Draft from the DICTIONARY DEFAULT: step 1 does not
    // supply `status`, so this is the platform's own value, not an echo of the test.
    chk('a new case defaults to Draft (status was never supplied on insert)', 'Draft', num.getValue('status'));
    chk('x_casemgmt_case.status carries the Draft dictionary default',
        'Draft', dict('x_casemgmt_case', 'status').getValue('default_value'));
    chk('Draft is the first selectable status choice', 'Draft', choices('x_casemgmt_case', 'status')[0]);
    // EXACT FIELD SET, not merely "the declared ones exist". Any column that is not
    // on this list - a stray field added by hand, a leftover from an experiment, an
    // accidental extra in a future payload - breaks the assertion by name.
    var CASE_FIELDS = ['assigned_agent', 'assigned_group', 'closed_date', 'description',
        'duration_to_close', 'number', 'opened_date', 'pending_reason', 'priority',
        'requester_email', 'requester_name', 'status', 'subject', 'type'];
    chk('x_casemgmt_case carries EXACTLY the declared field set',
        CASE_FIELDS.join(','), appElements('x_casemgmt_case').join(','));
    chk('x_casemgmt_case field count', String(CASE_FIELDS.length), String(appElements('x_casemgmt_case').length));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('x_casemgmt_case schema (AAP 0.5.7): checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'x_casemgmt_case schema (AAP 0.5.7)', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value>

    </sys_variable_value>
</unload>

// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so

(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();

    }

        d.query();
        while (d.next()) {
            var e = d.getValue('element');
            if (e && e.indexOf('sys_') !== 0) { out.push(e); }
        }
        out.sort();
        return out;
    }

    var TASK_SPEC = [
        ['case','reference',32,true,'x_casemgmt_case'], ['subject','string',255,true,''],
        ['type','string',40,false,''], ['status','string',40,false,''],
        ['assigned_to','reference',32,true,'sys_user'], ['due_date','glide_date',40,true,'']
    ];
    for (var i = 0; i < TASK_SPEC.length; i++) {
        var sp = TASK_SPEC[i], d = dict('x_casemgmt_case_task', sp[0]);
        chkTrue('x_casemgmt_case_task.' + sp[0] + ' exists', !!d);
        if (!d) continue;
        chk('x_casemgmt_case_task.' + sp[0] + ' type', sp[1], d.getValue('internal_type'));
        chk('x_casemgmt_case_task.' + sp[0] + ' max_length', sp[2], d.getValue('max_length'));

<unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00">
    <sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <document>sys_atf_step</document>
        <document_key>3c7766de1af36e9562517f2a8dd622a7</document_key>
        <order />
        <sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>2ec39e9bda5977ed74b1bcc616d46389</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "probe",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "cfdc67741a52236340f593d0229635a8",
            "prefix": "ATF-DM-01",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-DM-01 data model probe",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "priority": "Medium"
            }
        }
    ];

    // CLEANUP IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED.
    //
    // This step used to end with a "cleanup ran" check that compared the literal
    // string true against itself - a tautology. It therefore passed even when every
    // delete had
    // silently failed, so fixtures could survive and contaminate later steps, later
    // tests in the suite, and later runs (a stale pinned sys_id or a stale prefix row
    // makes another test assert against the wrong record). What follows checks the
    // outcome of each delete and then RE-QUERIES for residue, so a surviving row fails
    // this step and is named in the failure message.
    //
    // Note on coverage: a fixture carrying no `prefix` (case_party rows, which have no
    // `subject` column to match on) is swept by pinned sys_id only - the same guard the
    // delete loop uses - because that is the only key such a row is ever created with.
    var removed = 0, failedDeletes = [];
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) {
            old.setWorkflow(false);
            if (old.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[d].table + ':' + FIX[d].sys_id);
        }
    }
    for (var p = 0; p < FIX.length; p++) {
        if (!FIX[p].prefix) continue;
        var extra = new GlideRecord(FIX[p].table);
        extra.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[p].prefix);
        extra.query();
        while (extra.next()) {
            var extraId = extra.getUniqueValue();
            extra.setWorkflow(false);
            if (extra.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[p].table + ':' + extraId);
        }
    }
    chk('every delete reported success', '', failedDeletes.join(' | '));

    // Residue re-query: by pinned sys_id for every fixture, and by prefix for every
    // fixture that has one. Any row still present here is a real leak.
    var residue = [];
    for (var q = 0; q < FIX.length; q++) {
        var byId = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        if (byId.get(FIX[q].sys_id))
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' sys_id ' + FIX[q].sys_id + ' survived');
        if (!FIX[q].prefix) continue;
        var byPrefix = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        byPrefix.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[q].prefix);
        byPrefix.query();
        while (byPrefix.next())
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' ' + byPrefix.getUniqueValue() +
                ' [' + byPrefix.getValue('subject') + '] survived');
    }
    chk('no fixture residue remains after cleanup', '', residue.join(' | '));

    // setOutputMessage OVERWRITES rather than appends, so every reported
    // line is accumulated and emitted once, at the end of the step.
    var notes = [];
    notes.push('fixtures removed=' + removed +
        ' | deletes reporting failure=' + failedDeletes.length +
        ' | residue rows=' + residue.length);
    notes.push('fixture cleanup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture cleanup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value>

    </sys_variable_value>
</unload>

<unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00">
    <sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <document>sys_atf_step</document>
        <document_key>0c49d5628dca1cfa5a6de8db29fabe6e</document_key>
        <order />
        <sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>

        <sys_id>e609efad5a803801bd39d9050436ae96</sys_id>

        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "mine",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "6fab7dd278e415c8e5bdea665c89d8a5",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-02",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-02 manager fixture",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "unassigned",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "93eeda729062207211ec3270cbf1545e",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-02",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-02 unassigned fixture",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium"
            }
        }
    ];

    // A field value written as "@user:<user_name>" or "@group:<name>" is resolved
    // here, at run time, so no identity sys_id is baked into the test definition.
    function resolveToken(v) {
        if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.charAt(0) !== '@') { return v; }
        var sep = v.indexOf(':');
        var kind = v.substring(1, sep), key = v.substring(sep + 1);
        return kind === 'user' ? userId(key) : groupId(key);
    }
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) { old.setWorkflow(false); old.deleteRecord(); }
    }
    for (var f = 0; f < FIX.length; f++) {
        var gr = new GlideRecord(FIX[f].table);
        gr.initialize();
        gr.setNewGuidValue(FIX[f].sys_id);
        for (var fld in FIX[f].fields) gr.setValue(fld, resolveToken(FIX[f].fields[fld]));
        var newId = gr.insert();
        chk('fixture ' + FIX[f].label + ' created', FIX[f].sys_id, newId);
    }
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('fixture setup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture setup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value>

<unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00">
    <sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <document>sys_atf_step</document>
        <document_key>a1c14fa283b0aefe08da98ae10ac316f</document_key>

        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>a22ac5cff305f48751653920eeffff5c</sys_id>

        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }

    chk('impersonated user', 'x_casemgmt_demo_manager', gs.getUserName());
    chkTrue('manager holds x_casemgmt_case_manager', gs.hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager'));
    var probe = new GlideRecordSecure('x_casemgmt_case');
    chkTrue('manager can read the unassigned case', probe.get('93eeda729062207211ec3270cbf1545e'));
    chkTrue('manager canCreate', probe.canCreate());
    chkTrue('manager canRead', probe.canRead());
    chkTrue('manager canWrite', probe.canWrite());
    chkTrue('manager canDelete', probe.canDelete());
    // GlideRecordSecure.getRowCount() is NOT ACL-filtered - it reports the raw
    // database count - so ANY threshold assertion on it can pass while the role
    // sees nothing at all. Measured on this instance with 11 cases: the demo agent
    // (assigned-only) reported getRowCount()=11 while iteration yielded 9. The
    // visible set is therefore built by ITERATION and compared id-for-id against an
    // authoritative set read through a plain GlideRecord, which bypasses ACLs by
    // design and is the only trustworthy statement of what rows exist.
    function idsOf(gr) {
        var o = [];
        while (gr.next()) { o.push(gr.getUniqueValue()); }
        o.sort();
        return o;
    }
    var authoritative = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    authoritative.query();
    var everyId = idsOf(authoritative);
    var secureAll = new GlideRecordSecure('x_casemgmt_case');
    secureAll.query();
    var visibleId = idsOf(secureAll);
    chk('manager sees EVERY case (read all, exact set equality)',
        everyId.join(','), visibleId.join(','));
    chk('manager visible-case count equals the stored row count',
        String(everyId.length), String(visibleId.length));
    chkTrue('the ASSIGNED fixture is inside the manager visible set',
        visibleId.indexOf('6fab7dd278e415c8e5bdea665c89d8a5') > -1);
    chkTrue('the UNASSIGNED fixture is inside the manager visible set',
        visibleId.indexOf('93eeda729062207211ec3270cbf1545e') > -1);
    chkTrue('the comparison is not being made over an almost-empty table (AAP 0.7.4 seeds 10+)',
        everyId.length >= 10);
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('manager capability matrix: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'manager capability matrix', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value>

    </sys_variable_value>
</unload>

<unload unload_date="2025-01-01 00:00:00">
    <sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <document>sys_atf_step</document>
        <document_key>e90c61d173abe3dab56bf756d7bc021a</document_key>
        <order />
